§ 805.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   ADULT ARCADE means an establishment where, for any form of
consideration, one or more still or motion picture projectors, slide projectors
or similar machines, or other image producing machines, for viewing by five or
fewer people each, are regularly used to show films, motion pictures, video
cassettes, slides or other photographic reproductions which constitute adult
material.
   (b)    ADULT BOOKSTORE means any establishment deriving a majority of its
gross income from the sale or rental of, or having as a significant and
substantial portion of its stock in trade in, books, magazines or other
periodicals, films or mechanical or nonmechanical devices, which constitute
adult material.
      (1)   When such bookstores offer sexually oriented materials, such
materials shall be displayed in such a manner as to protect persons under 21
years of age from exposure to them.
      (2)   Where sexually oriented materials occupy more than 10% but less
than 40% of floor space, such materials shall be kept in a separate room in
which only persons 21 years or older may gain access through doors mechanically
controlled by an attendant.
   (c)    ADULT CABARET means a commercial establishment, including a
nightclub, bar, restaurant or similar establishment which features dancers,
strippers, or similar live entertainers who expose specified anatomical areas
or who depict or describe specified sexual activities.
   (d)    ADULT ENTERTAINMENT ESTABLISHMENT means any adult arcade, adult
bookstore, adult motel, adult theater, adult video store, adult cabaret, peep
show, sex shop or other adults-only establishment.
   (e)    ADULT MATERIAL means any book, magazine, newspaper, pamphlet, poster,
print, picture, slide, transparency, figure, image, depiction, motion picture
film, phonographic record or tape, or other tangible thing, or any service
capable of arousing interest through sight, sound or touch, and:
      (1)   Which material is distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on
matter displaying, describing or representing sexual activity, masturbation,
sexual excitement, nudity, bestiality or human bodily functions or elimination
or
      (2)   Which service is distinguished by an emphasis on sexual activity,
masturbation, sexual excitement, nudity, bestiality or human bodily functions
or elimination.
   (f)   ADULT MOTEL means a motel, hotel or similar commercial establishment
which:
      (1)    Offers public accommodations, for any form of consideration, and
provides patrons with closed circuit television transmissions, films, motion
pictures, video cassettes, slides or other photographic reproductions which
constitute adult material and
      (2)    Advertises the availability of such adult materials by means of a
sign visible from the public right-of-way, or by means of any off premises
advertising, including, but not limited to, newspapers, magazines, radio or
television.
   (g)    ADULT THEATER means an enclosed building or motion picture drive-in
theater used for presenting, and deriving a majority of its gross income from,
or having as a significant and substantial portion of its stock in trade in,
films which constitute adult material for observation by patrons at said
theater.
   (h)   ADULT VIDEO STORE means an establishment deriving a majority of its
gross income from, or having a substantial or significant portion of its stock
in trade in, videos which constitute adult material.
      (1)   When such video store offers sexually oriented materials, such
materials shall be displayed in such a manner as to protect persons under 21
years of age from exposure to them.
      (2)    Where sexually oriented materials occupy more than 10% but less
than 40% of floor space, such materials shall be kept in a separate room in
which only persons 21 years or older may gain access through doors mechanically
controlled by an attendant.
   (i)   EMPLOYEE or EMPLOYMENT includes employees, independent contractors,
and agents, whether compensated or not.
   (j)    NUDITY means the showing of the human male or female genitals, pubic
area or buttocks, with less than a fully opaque covering the showing of the
female breast, with less than a fully opaque covering of the nipple and areola
or the showing of the covered male genitals in a discernibly turgid state. The
covering of the nipple and areola shall not be made to appear as the bare or
exposed nipple and areola of the female breast.
   (k)    OTHER ADULTS ONLY ESTABLISHMENT means an establishment which features
services which constitute adult material, or which features exhibitions of
persons totally nude or topless and/or bottomless, male or female
impersonators, or similar entertainment which constitutes adult material.
   (l)   PEEP SHOW means an establishment used for presenting video materials
or live shows characterized by an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, or
relating specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas for
observation by patrons in individual viewing booths.
   (m)   SEX SHOP means an establishment:
      (1)   Offering for sale items from any two of the following categories:
sexually oriented books and videos, lingerie; leather goods marketed or
presented in a context to suggest their use for "bondage" or other sexual
activities;
      (2)   Offering for sale sexually oriented toys or novelties;
      (3)   Devoting more than 40% of floor space to sexually oriented
magazines, books, videos, or other media; or
      (4)   Advertising or holding itself out in any form a "XXX," "adult,"
"sex," or otherwise as a sexually oriented business.
   (n)   SPECIFIED SEXUAL ACTIVITIES as used in the adult entertainment
establishment descriptions above means:
      (1)   Human genitals in a state of sexual stimulation or arousal;
      (2)   Acts, real or simulated, of human masturbation, sexual intercourse,
sodomy, cunnilingus or fellatio; and
      (3)   Fondling or other erotic touching of human genitals, pubic regions,
buttocks or female breasts.
   (o)   SPECIFIED ANATOMICAL AREAS as used in the adult entertainment
establishment descriptions above means:
      (1)   Less than completely and opaquely covered human genitals, pubic
regions, buttocks and female breasts below a point immediately above the top of
the areola; and
      (2)   Human male genitals in a discernibly turgid state even if
completely and opaquely covered.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.02 SCOPE OF REGULATIONS.
   These regulations govern adult entertainment establishments within the
incorporated area of the City of Middletown, Ohio, and the owners, operators,
persons in charge, and employees of such establishments.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.03 LEGISLATIVE FINDINGS.
   The City Council of the City of Middletown makes the following legislative
findings in support of this regulation of adult entertainment establishments:
   (a)   Surveys conducted for neighboring communities and conducted by and/or
for various municipalities throughout the country concerning the secondary
effects of adult entertainment establishments provide substantial evidence that
such establishments have a deleterious effect on adjacent residential areas,
including the downgrade of property values and increase in crime;
   (b)   Adult entertainment establishments are used for unlawful sexual
activities, including prostitution and sexual liaison of a casual nature;
   (c)   Adult entertainment establishments pose potential harmful effects on
minors exposed to such establishments and their secondary effects;
   (d)   Adult entertainment establishments have serious objectionable
operational characteristics and, therefore, require special supervision from
public safety and other agencies of the City to protect and preserve the
health, safety and welfare of the patrons of such establishments and the
citizens of the City; and
   (e)   City Council desires to minimize and control these adverse secondary
effects so as to protect its citizens from increased crime, preserve the
property values and character of surrounding neighborhoods, deter the spread of
urban blight, and protect minors from the possible harmful effects of such
establishments.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.04 PURPOSE.
   (a)   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate adult entertainment
establishments to:
      (1)   Promote the health, safety, morals and general welfare of the
citizens of Middletown, Ohio;
      (2)   Establish reasonable and uniform regulations for the operation of
adult entertainment facilities with the goal of reducing or eliminating the
adverse secondary effects associated with such facilities; and
      (3)   To protect minors, by reason of age, from exposure to unsuitable or
sexually oriented materials.
   (b)   It is not the intent of this chapter to limit or restrict the content
of communicative materials, including sexually oriented materials. Similarly,
it is not the intent or effect of this chapter to restrict or deny access to
materials protected by the First Amendment, or to deny access by the
distributors and exhibitors of sexually oriented entertainment to their
intended market. The purpose of this regulation is to impose content neutral
time, place and manner restrictions designed to the public health, safety and
welfare, while not unreasonably limiting avenues of communication.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.05 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (a)    No person shall own, operate or participate in the operation of an
adult entertainment establishment, nor shall any premises be erected, altered,
used, arranged or designed to be used in whole or in part as an adult
entertainment establishment, unless the owner or person in control of the
premises where such establishment shall be located first obtains a valid and
current permit for the operation of an adult entertainment establishment.
   (b)    A separate permit is required for each location of an adult
entertainment establishment. The permit shall be prominently displayed on the
premises in an area open to the public. A permit issued pursuant to this
chapter shall be valid for a period of one year from the date of its issuance.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.06 APPLICATION FOR PERMIT.
   (a)    In order to obtain a permit, an application must be submitted by the
owner or person in control of the premises where the adult entertainment
establishment is to be located.
   (b)    An application for an original license must be submitted in writing,
addressed to the Chief of Police of the City of Middletown. The application
shall include:
      (1)    A nonrefundable filing fee in the amount of five hundred dollars
($500.00);
      (2)    The address of the premises where the adult entertainment
establishment will be operated;
      (3)    The full name, address, social security number and date of birth
of the applicant. If the applicant is a partnership, a limited partnership or a
corporation, the name of the entity the status of the entity the state under
which it is organized the address of its principal office and its principal
office in Ohio, if different and its Federal employer identification number. If
the applicant is a corporation, the name and address of its statutory agent in
Ohio. If the applicant is a partnership, the full name, residence address, date
of birth and social security number of each partner, the status of each
partner, and whether the partnership has complied with Ohio R.C. 1777.02
(fictitious name statute);
      (4)    The full name, address, date of birth and social security number
of the person to be responsible for the operation of the adult entertainment
establishment for which a permit is sought;
      (5)   A statement that the applicant and, to the applicant's knowledge,
the person named in response to division (b)(4) hereof, have never been
convicted of or pleaded guilty to any offense other than a misdemeanor traffic
offense, or a statement listing the offenses other than misdemeanor traffic
offenses of which the applicant or the other person named in the application
has been convicted, including the offense, the date of conviction and the name
and location of the court;
      (6)    A statement by the applicant for a permit to operate an adult
entertainment establishment that the Ohio Liquor Control Commission has never,
pursuant to Ohio R.C. 4301.25 or any similar statute, law or municipal code
from another state, revoked a permit held by the applicant or any person or
entity named in the application and;
      (7)    A plat of the property described in division (b)(2) hereof,
showing the property lines, building locations, parking areas, entry ways and
lighting systems, buffering and fire protection services.
   (c)    All applicants shall execute an authorization for an investigation
into the background of the applicant and any person or entity named in the
application.
   (d)   All applicants shall execute a statement agreeing to abide by these
regulations and laws of Ohio, and any amendments, additions, or reenactment
thereof.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.07 INVESTIGATION.
   Upon receipt of any application for a permit or renewal permit to operate an
adult entertainment establishment, the Chief of the Division of Police shall
conduct an investigation into the background of the applicant and into the
background of other persons or entities named in the application. A written
report of the results of the investigation shall be prepared by the
investigating officer or agency and shall become part of the application for a
permit.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.08 ACTION ON APPLICATION FOR PERMIT AND RENEWAL PERMIT.
   (a)   The Chief of Police shall approve the application within 15 working
days unless:
      (1)   It is incomplete or contains false information; or
      (2)    The applicant is an entity not in good standing where it is
organized, or not authorized to do business in the State of Ohio; or
      (3)   The reports of any agency reveal the premises to be unhealthy,
unsafe or hazardous, or in violation of health or safety codes; or
      (4)    The applicant or the person proposed to operate the adult
entertainment establishment covered by the permit is under 18 years of age; or
      (5)    The applicant or person operating the adult entertainment
establishment has violated, or the proposed operation would violate, any
provision of this chapter; or
      (6)    The applicant or any other person named in the application has
been convicted or pleaded guilty to an offense listed in Ohio R.C. Chapter
2907, or a substantially equivalent offense under a municipal ordinance in the
State of Ohio or under the laws of another state, within the past five years;
or
      (7)   The applicant or any other person named in the application for an
initial or renewal permit to operate an adult entertainment establishment or
any person employed or acting as an agent or independent contractor at the
adult entertainment establishment, has been convicted or plead guilty to a
violation of Ohio R.C. 503.53(C) or any similar municipal ordinance within the
past five years; or
      (8)   The operation of the adult entertainment establishment would
violate existing zoning ordinances.
   (b)    If the Chief of Police finds that none of the eight conditions in §
805.08(a) exists, he shall promptly issue to the applicant a permit within
three working days after approval.
   (c)   If the Chief of Police determines that any one or more of the eight
conditions in §
805.08(a) exists, he shall forward the complete application file to the City of
Middletown Citizens Advisory Board ("Board") for hearing and determination. The
Board shall conduct a public hearing on the application, during a special
meeting to be held within ten working days after receiving the application
file. The applicant shall have the opportunity to present information,
evidence, and testimony to the Board, at the public hearing regarding the
application. If the permit is denied, the Board shall promptly notify (within
three working days of their determination) the applicant in writing of its
decision denying the application. If the Board approves the application, the
Chief of Police shall promptly issue to the applicant a permit within three
working days after the Board's decision. In no circumstance shall the action of
the Chief of Police and/or the Board, in granting or denying the permit, be
more than 45 working days from the filing of the application and submission of
the items required to be provided by the applicant as provided in §
805.06. A continuance, granted at the request of the applicant, tolls the time
requirements of this section, for the duration of the requested continuance.
The failure of the Chief of Police and the Board to act within the 45 working
day period shall constitute a grant of the permit.
   (d)   A permit or renewal permit to operate an adult entertainment
establishment shall contain the address of the permit premises, the name and
address of the permit holder, and the date of issuance and the date of
expiration of the permit.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.09 RENEWAL OF PERMIT.
   (a)   A permit to operate an adult entertainment establishment is valid for
one year and expires on the anniversary of the date of issuance, unless a
permitee has applied for a renewal permit or unless the permit was revoked as
provided in this chapter.
   (b)   An application to renew a previously issued permit shall include a
nonrefundable fee of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) and any changes in the
information provided in the initial application. The application shall include
the names, addresses and dates of birth of all employees of the adult
entertainment establishment. The application for renewal must be filed not
later than 30 days prior to the expiration of the existing permit. An
application for renewal shall be investigated and reviewed using the same
standards and time requirements delineated in §
805.08.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.10 REVOCATION OF PERMIT.
   The Chief of Police may, upon discovery of a violation of this chapter, or
on any of the same grounds listed in §
805.08(b) for denial of the permit, including any such grounds arising or
discovered after the issuance of a permit, set a public revocation hearing to
be conducted before the Board not later than 15 working days after the notice
of the violation to the permittee. The Chief of Police shall promptly notify
the permittee in writing of the date and time of the public hearing and the
grounds for revocation. At the public hearing the Board shall allow the
permittee to present evidence regarding the alleged violation. Pursuant to the
notice and at the conclusion of the hearing the Board may dismiss or sustain
the allegations. The Board may revoke the permit upon a finding of a violation
of these regulations. The Board will publicly announce the decision and will
direct the Chief of Police to notify the permittees of the decision by
certified mail, mailed within three working days of the close of the hearing.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.11 PROMPT JUDICIAL REVIEW.
   (a)   In the event that the Board does not renew a permit or revokes an
issued permit, the permittee may continue to operate his or her establishment
for such time as is required to appeal the denial of the permit renewal to a
court of law and request a stay of proceedings. After the passage of 60 days
from the failure of the Board to renew a permit or from the date of permit
revocation, the permittee shall discontinue operating the adult entertainment
establishment if a court has not granted a requested stay. During the appeal
process, the applicant shall be required to follow all guidelines set forth in
this Chapter.
   (b)   Upon the appeal of the denial of a permit to the Common Pleas Court
pursuant to Ohio R.C. Chapter 2506, the City shall file a transcript of the
proceedings before the Board with the Court within 20 days of receiving the
notice of appeal.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.12 TRANSFER OF PERMIT.
   A permittee shall not transfer the permit to a location other than the
premises designated in the application. A permittee shall not transfer the
permit to any other person or entity.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.13 RESTRICTIONS ON OPERATION.
   Adult entertainment establishments shall be permitted in those zoning
classifications as in which the underlying activity is a permitted use, unless
otherwise established by the zoning ordinances of the City of Middletown, Ohio.
Adult entertainment establishment are subject to the following additional
restrictions:
   (a)    Adult entertainment establishments shall close not later than 12:00
midnight and shall not reopen earlier than 12:00 noon.
   (b)   No adult entertainment establishment shall be established and/or
operated within a radius of 500 feet of any area where residences are zoned as
a permitted use.
   (c)   No adult entertainment establishment shall be established and/or
operated within a radius of 1,000 feet of any church, permanently established
place of worship, school, hospital, library, public playground or public park.
   (d)   No adult entertainment establishment shall be established and/or
operated in a structure which is attached or adjacent to any hotel, motel or
other establishment which offers sleeping rooms for let on a daily or less than
daily basis.
   (e)   (1)   No adult entertainment establishment shall be established and/or
operated within a radius of 250 feet of another adult entertainment
establishment.
      (2)   All distances in this division shall be measured in a straight
line, without regard to intervening structures or objects from the nearest
point of the property line where the adult entertainment establishment is
conducted, to the nearest point of the property line of the residential zone,
predominantly residential area, church, permanently established place of
worship, school, hospital, library, public playground, public park, or other
adult entertainment establishment.
   (f)    No advertisements, displays or other promotional materials shall be
shown or exhibited to be visible to the public from pedestrian sidewalks or
walkways or from other areas, public or semipublic.
   (g)   All building openings, entries, windows, etc., for adult uses shall be
located, covered, or serviced to prevent a view into the interior from any
public or semipublic area, sidewalk, or street. For new construction, the
building shall be oriented so as to minimize any possibility of viewing the
interior from public or semipublic areas.
   (h)   No screens, loudspeakers or sound equipment shall be used for adult
motion picture theaters (enclosed or drive-in) that can be seen or discerned by
the public from public or semipublic areas.
   (i)   Off street parking shall be provided in accordance with zoning
requirements for similar uses.
   (j)   No person under 18 years of age shall be employed by or serve as an
agent or independent contractor for the adult entertainment establishment,
whether fulltime or part time, and regardless of whether such individual is
compensated in any manner.
   (k)   The permittee shall file a list of employees with the Chief of Police,
and shall file an amended list at any time there is a change in personnel
(within 20 calendar days of any change). The list shall state the name, date of
birth, and position of each employee.
   (l)   The owner, operator, or person in charge of the adult entertainment
establishment shall exercise adequate supervision to insure that the employees,
agents and independent contractors comply at all times with these regulations
and the laws of Ohio.
   (m)   All off street parking areas and premises entries of the business
shall be illuminated from dusk until closing hours of operations with a
lighting system which provide an average maintained horizontal illumination of
one (1.0) foot candle of light on the parking surface.
   (n)   The permittee shall not allow any portion of the interior premises to
be visible from outside the premises.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.14 RULES GOVERNING CONDUCT WITHIN AN ADULT ENTERTAINMENT ESTABLISHMENT.
   (a)   A person under the age of 18 shall not accept or continue employment
by or in an adult entertainment establishment in any capacity, whether full-
time or part-time, and with or without remuneration or compensation in any
form.
   (b)   No person shall accept or continue employment by any adult
entertainment establishment that does not have a valid, current permit issued
pursuant to these regulations.
   (c)   Any employee of an adult entertainment establishment shall cooperate
with any background investigation permitted under these regulations.
   (d)    No employee, independent contractor or agent of an adult
entertainment establishment shall, in the performance of his or her duties, do
any of the following:
      (1)    Appear in a state of nudity, as that term is defined in §
805.01;
      (2)    Place his or her hand upon, or touch with any part of his or her
body, the genitals, pubic area or buttocks of any other person, or the breasts
of any female; and
      (3)    Perform or offer to perform any act that would require the
touching of the genitals, pubic area or buttocks of any other person, or the
breasts of any female.
   (e)   Any adult entertainment establishment offering live dancing
performances shall conform to the following requirements:
      (1)   The dancing performance shall be confined to a clearly defined
stage or platform area that is elevated at least two feet above the normal
floor elevation of the establishment.
      (2)   There shall be a clearly defined and delineated six-foot buffer
area or space between the aforesaid stage or platform and any area of the
establishment in which customers are customarily seated and/or served.
      (3)    Said buffer zone shall be clearly and permanently delineated by
rail, rope, enclosure or other similar means.
      (4)    All dancing or entertainment shall be confined to the stage or
platform area as defined herein.
      (5)   At no time during the performance shall the patrons or the
entertainer be permitted to encroach on the aforedescribed buffer zone.
      (6)    Patrons are prohibited from commingling with or touching the
entertainers on the stage or platform.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.15 PUBLIC NUISANCE.
   An adult entertainment establishment, operating without a valid permit, as
required by this chapter, is hereby declared to be a public nuisance, subject
to abatement in accordance with State and local law. Such abatement shall be in
addition to the criminal sanctions provided herein. Such abatement shall be in
addition to all other civil actions and sanctions available at law.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.16 SEVERABILITY.
   Should any section or provision of this chapter be declared by the courts to
be unconstitutional or invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of
this Section as a whole, or any part thereof, other than the part so declared
to be unconstitutional or invalid.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)
§ 805.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Owner or Person in Control. 
      (1)   Any owner or person in control of a premises who knowingly
operates, participates in the operation or permits the operation of an adult
entertainment establishment without a permit as required by this chapter is
guilty of operating an adult entertainment establishment without a permit, a
misdemeanor of the first degree, and shall be fined not more than one thousand
dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned for not more than six months, or both, for each
offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
      (2)   Any owner or operation of an adult entertainment establishment who
violates this any portion of this Chapter while; a) operating an adult
entertainment establishment under a permit issued under this Chapter, b)
appealing a denied renewal application, or c) who is awaiting appeal while
operating under a permit which has been revoked, is guilty of a misdemeanor of
the fourth degree, and shall be fined not more than two hundred and fifty
dollars ($250) or imprisoned for not more than 30 days, or both for each
violation. A separate offense shall be deemed committed for each individual
violation of this chapter and a separate offense shall be deemed committed for
each day during which a violation or noncompliance continues.
   (b)   Employees, Agents and Independent Contractors of Adult Entertainment
Establishments. Employees, independent contractors and agents who violate the
provisions contained within §
805.14 shall be guilty of a minor misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to
one hundred and fifty dollars ($150.00). A separate offense shall be deemed
committed for each individual violation of §
805.14 and a separate offense shall be deemed committed for each day during
which a violation or noncompliance continues.
   (c)   Patrons of Adult Entertainment Establishments. Patrons of adult
entertainment establishments who violate §
805.14 (e) (6) by commingling or touching entertainers shall be guilty of a
minor misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to one hundred and fifty dollars
($150.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed for each individual
violation of this section.
(Ord. O2007-18, passed 2-20-2007)

pass or distribute handbills, cards, papers, posters, placards, written or

merchandise or any other advertising literature, or throw the same into any
automobile, wagon or other vehicle, whether such vehicle is upon a street or
other public place in the City or upon private property, or pass the same from
hand to hand to any person upon a street or in any other public place in the
City. This division shall not apply to magazines, newspapers or any publication
distributed by United States mail.
   (b)   The written permission of the City Manager required in division (a)
hereof shall only be granted after an application in writing is filed with the
City Manager by the person seeking such permission.
   (c)   No person shall employ, hire or cause to be hired or employed any
person to distribute handbills, papers, cards, placards, printed or written,
designed or used for the advertisement of goods, wares and merchandise in
violation of any of the provisions of this section.
   (d)   No person shall throw, drop, discard or place handbills, cards,
papers, posters, placards, written or printed, designed and used for the
purpose of advertising goods, wares and merchandise, or any other advertising
literature, or any other handbills, cards, papers, posters and placards upon
any of the streets or other public places in the City.

CHAPTER 813: CABLE TELEVISION SYSTEMS
Section
813.01   Scope; application of chapter; amendments.
813.02   Filing and review of rate schedules.
813.03   Utilization of rate consultants; payment of costs of review by
operators.
813.04   Adoption of FCC Customer Service Standards.
CROSS REFERENCES
   Cable television contracts - see Ohio R.C. 505.90 et seq.
   Interrupting or impairing television service - see Ohio R.C. 2909.04
   “Property” defined to include cable television service - see GEN. OFF.
606.01(o)
   “Services” defined to include cable television service - see GEN. OFF.
642.01(a), (r)
§ 813.01 SCOPE; APPLICATION OF CHAPTER; AMENDMENTS.
   (a)   All rates and charges for basic cable service and any other cable
programming services, as defined by the Cable Television Consumer Protection
and Competition Act of 1992 (“the Act”) and applicable Federal Communications
Commission (FCC) regulations, shall, to the extent permissible as provided in
such Act and regulations, be subject to regulation by the City in the manner
provided by this chapter. This chapter shall apply to all cable television
system operators in the City. The operator of a cable television system
operating in the City shall be subject to the rate regulation provisions
provided for herein and those of the FCC provided in Title 47 C.F.R. part
76.900, subpart N.
   (b)   The City reserves the right to amend this chapter from time to time,
consistent with the requirements of the FCC and State and Federal law.
(Ord. O93-116, passed 11-16-1993)
§ 813.02 FILING AND REVIEW OF RATE SCHEDULES.
   (a)   Adoption of FCC Rules by City. The City hereby adopts and shall follow
the rules relating to cable television rate regulation promulgated by the FCC
provided in Title 47 C.F.R. part 76.900, subpart N. Prior to approving or
disapproving any rates, the City shall provide an opportunity for consideration
of the views of interested parties.
   (b)   Notice to operators of City’s certification. Upon adoption of this
chapter, the Clerk of the City Council will send each operator of a cable
television system in the City, via certified mail, return receipt requested, a
written notice, which shall include a copy of this chapter and the time-stamped
copy of Form 328.
   (c)   Submission of rate and benchmark information; approval or disapproval
of rates. Within 30 days after receipt of the aforesaid notice, a cable
television operator shall have 30 days to respond with rate and benchmark
information utilizing FCC Form 393 - Determination of Maximum Initial Permitted
Rates for Regulated Cable Services and Actual Cost of Equipment.
      (1)   If the initial rates and/or any subsequent rate increases are
within the FCC’s standards, the rates will be effective 30 days after
submission.
      (2)   If the City is unable to determine whether the rate at issue is
within the FCC’s standards based on the material before it, or if the cable
operator has submitted a cost-of-service showing seeking to justify a rate
above the FCC’s reasonable rate level, the City may take an additional period
of time to make a final determination and toll the effective date of the
proposed rates for a commensurate period.
         A.   The City may take an additional 90 days if it needs more time to
ensure that a rate is within the FCC’s rate standards.
         B.   The City may take an additional 150 days to evaluate a cost-of-
service showing seeking to justify a rate above the reasonable rate level.
         C.   The City must issue a brief written decision regarding its
invocation of the additional time period.
      (3)   In all cases, the City will issue a written decision to approve the
rate schedule, disapprove the rate schedule or continue for review.
      (4)   If rates are in excess of the FCC’s standards, the rates may be
reduced by the City pursuant to applicable FCC regulations.
   (d)   Filing of additional rate changes. After the initial rate schedule
procedures are followed as provided in this section, the cable operator shall,
in conjunction with each change in the rates and charges applicable to basic
cable service, conform to the standards of the FCC. Before any rate change is
effective, the cable operator shall notify the City of its requested rate
change by giving the City 30 days advance written notice before the change is
effective and by providing the City with its rates and applicable information
pursuant to FCC regulations.
   (e)   Appeals. To the extent specifically permitted by Federal law and
applicable FCC rules, the cable operator shall be permitted to appeal to the
FCC for a review of the decision of the City.
(Ord. O93-116, passed 11-16-1993)
§ 813.03 UTILIZATION OF RATE CONSULTANTS; PAYMENT OF COSTS OF REVIEW BY
OPERATORS.
   (a)   The City may utilize a rate consultant to advise it on proposed rate
changes and to assist it in the procedures and the standards for review adopted
by the FCC. A rate consultant may be any person who has sufficient background
and experience, in the sole opinion of the City, to properly evaluate and
analyze rates and charges.
   (b)   All costs for the review of initial rates or rate changes shall be
paid by the cable operator upon demand of the City, unless contrary to
applicable rules of the FCC governing these procedures or unless otherwise
specifically preempted by State or Federal law. The costs shall include, but
not be limited to, rate consultants, attorneys’ fees and the reasonable value
of services (as determined by the City) rendered by the City or any City
employees, agents or representatives.
(Ord. O93-116, passed 11-16-1993)
§ 813.04 ADOPTION OF FCC CUSTOMER SERVICE STANDARDS.
   (a)   The City hereby adopts the Customer Service Standards enacted by the
FCC on March 11, 1993, through FCC Order 93-15, MM Docket No. 92-263, Appendix
B, a copy of which is attached to original Ord. O93-95, passed October 5, 1993,
and incorporated herein by reference. Said standards shall be in addition to
the customer service regulations in the current franchise agreement with TCI
Cablevision, Inc., and shall be made a part of said franchise agreement as if
rewritten therein. In the event of any conflict between FCC standards and the
customer service regulations contained in a current franchise agreement, the
more stringent standard or regulation shall govern.
   (b)   Any violation of the Customer Service Standards adopted herein shall
be governed by the penalty provision of the current franchise agreement with
TCI Cablevision, Inc.
   (c)   The Clerk of the City Council is directed to immediately notify TCI
Cablevision, Inc., of the adoption of this section and the City’s intent to
enforce the FCC Customer Service Standards. Notice shall be in writing,
delivered by certified mail, in accordance with the notice provisions of the
FCC standards and the current franchise agreement with TCI Cablevision, Inc.
   (d)   The Customer Service Standards adopted herein shall be in full force
and effect commencing on the ninety-first day following the aforesaid notice to
TCI Cablevision, Inc.
   (e)   Adoption of these minimum Customer Service Standards shall not
preclude the City from adopting additional reasonable customer service
regulations or consumer protection laws which the City may determine to be
necessary to ensure that the citizens of the City who subscribe to cable
television are appropriately protected in their relationship with the City’s
cable television franchise holder.
(Ord. O93-95, passed 10-5-1993)

§ 814.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   AMUSEMENT DEVICE. Any machine, device or contrivance, including a
pinball machine, that permits a game to be played by the insertion of a coin,
slug, token, plate or disc, or by the payment of a fee or anything of value,
that is operated for amusement only and does not dispense any form of prize,
reward or thing of value and does not contain within itself the means to
record, or does not in any other manner attempt to record games played.
   (b)   PINBALL MACHINE. A machine, device or contrivance that permits a game
to be played by the insertion of a coin, slug, token, plate or disc, or by the
payment of a fee or anything of value, the object of which game is to propel
any number of balls or marbles onto a board or other surface within the device
for the purpose of having such balls or marbles, rolling upon such surface,
strike any number of targets thereon or enter any number of slots therein,
either of which will register or accumulate a score for the player.
(Ord. O93-46, passed 5-18-1993)
§ 814.02 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall display or keep for public patronage any amusement device
without first having obtained a license therefor from the City for each such
device.
(Ord. 3995, passed 12-18-1963)
§ 814.03 CONTENTS AND DISPLAY OF LICENSE.
   The license required in §
814.02 shall bear the name of the licensee, the date of issuance, a brief
description of the device, the manufacturer’s serial number which appears on
the device, the place where the device will be situated, and a facsimile of the
City Manager’s signature. The license shall be attached to the device at all
times in a conspicuous place in such a manner that it cannot be removed by
anyone other than the licensee.
(Ord. 3995, passed 12-18-1963)
§ 814.04 LICENSE FEE.
   Effective December 1, 1993, the fee for the license required in §
814.02 shall be one hundred dollars ($100.00) per year for each device. If the
license is issued for a shorter term than one year, such fee shall be prorated
at the rate of one-twelfth of such amount per month or part thereof. The fee
for the transfer of a licensed device from one location to another shall be
twenty-five dollars ($25.00).
(Ord. O93-46, passed 5-18-1993)
§ 814.05 EFFECTIVE PERIOD; TRANSFERABILITY.
   Each license required in §
814.02 shall expire on November 30 next following the date of issue. No person
shall transfer such license from one device to another, or from one person to
another. No person shall transfer a licensed device from one location to
another without having first paid the transfer fee set forth in §
814.04.
(Ord. O81-76, passed 5-19-1981)
§ 814.06 PRIZES TO PLAYERS.
   No person shall give any prize, award, merchandise, gift or anything else of
value to any player of an amusement device for having obtained a certain score
or for any other achievement on account of such play.
(Ord. 3995, passed 12-18-1963)
§ 814.07 PINBALL MACHINES EXCEPTED. (REPEALED)
Editor’s note:
   Section 814.07 was repealed by Ord. O93-46, passed May 18, 1993.
§ 814.99 PENALTY.
Editor’s note:
   See §
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.

§ 816.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter and in other ordinances relating to the same
subject:
   (a)   PUBLIC DANCE. Any dance to which admission may be had by the payment,
directly or indirectly, of a fee, or any dance to which the public generally
may gain admission with or without the payment of a fee, provided that a dance
given by a bona fide religious, charitable or fraternal organization for its
members only and their families shall not be included.
   (b)   PUBLIC DANCE HALL. Any room, place or space in which a public dance is
held, except the hall or quarters of a bona fide religious, charitable or

shall be refunded if such license is revoked.
(Ord. O81-75, passed 5-19-1981)
§ 816.04 EFFECTIVE PERIOD; TRANSFERABILITY.
   Each license required in §
816.02 shall expire on January 31 next following the date of issue. No such
license shall be transferable as to locations.
§ 816.05 QUALIFICATIONS OF LICENSEE; REFERRAL TO CHIEF OF POLICE.
   (a)   The license required in §
816.02 shall not be issued to any applicant therefor who has within the six
months preceding his application for such license been convicted of the
violation of any law or ordinance regulating or pertaining to public dance
halls or public dances, or the violation of any of the provisions of Chapters
612, 624 or 666 of Part Six - the General Offenses Code, or an existing or
former municipal ordinance or law of this or any other state or the United
States substantially equivalent to such provisions. Such license shall also not
be granted if within the six months preceding the application therefor any
similar license held by such applicant has been revoked.
(Adopting Ordinance)
   (b)   Such license shall not be issued until the application therefor has
been referred to the Chief of Police, and he reports that there is no objection
under the provisions of division (a) hereof to its issuance.
(Ord. 2093, passed 8-16-1934)
§ 816.06 DANCE PERMIT.
   (a)   Required. No person not the holder of the public dance hall license
required in §
816.02 shall hold or conduct a public dance without first having obtained a
permit therefor from the City Manager.
   (b)   Application; issuance; fee. Such permit shall not be issued unless
application therefor has been made at least 48 hours before the time such
public dance is to be held or conducted. If such public dance is not to be held
or conducted in a licensed public dance hall, the issuance of any permit
therefor shall be subject to all the provisions of §§
816.02 through 816.05 in like manner as for such public dance hall license,

the provisions of this chapter or any other ordinance, law or regulation in
respect to dance halls, or any of the provisions of Chapters 612, 624, 630, 648
or 666 of Part Six - the General Offenses Code, is being violated.
§ 816.08 PROHIBITED ACTS.

fee charged to a public dance; or

for instructions in dancing when in fact it is a public dance.

§ 818.01 DISTRESS MERCHANDISE SALE DEFINED.
   DISTRESS MERCHANDISE SALE. Any offer to sell to the public, or sale to the
public of goods, wares or merchandise on the implied or direct representation
that such sale is in anticipation of the termination of a business at its
present location or that the sale is being held other than in the ordinary
course of business. Without limiting the generality of this definition,
distress merchandise sale includes any sale advertised either specifically or
in substance to be a fire sale, smoke and water damage sale, liquidation sale,
adjustment sale, creditor’s sale, trustee’s sale, bankrupt sale, save us from
bankruptcy sale, insolvent sale, insurance salvage sale, mortgage sale,
assignee’s sale, adjuster’s sale, must vacate sale, quitting business sale,
forced out of business sale, removal sale, whether by auction or otherwise.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.02 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall advertise or conduct a distress merchandise sale without
first having obtained a license therefor as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.03 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   (a)   Every person requiring a distress merchandise sale license shall make
application in writing to the City Manager at least 15 days prior to
commencement of the sale. Each application shall be sworn to before a person
authorized to administer oaths and shall contain the following information and
such other information as the City Manager deems necessary:
      (1)   The name and address of owner of the business and merchandise;
      (2)   The designation of the place where the sale is to be held;
      (3)   The nature of the occupancy of the place where the sale is to be
held, whether by lease or otherwise and the effective date of the termination
of such occupancy;
      (4)   A full and complete statement regarding the distress merchandise
sale, including the reason for such sale, the hours and days during which the
sale will be held and the commencement and termination date of the sale;
      (5)   A complete and detailed inventory of the goods, wares and
merchandise to be sold at such sale, including a list of the merchandise on
order and that merchandise received during the 15 days preceding the filing of
the application. The inventory shall contain a sworn statement of the cost and
retail value of the goods, wares and merchandise; and
      (6)   A statement that the applicant in making his or her application
agrees to admit the examiners appointed pursuant to §
818.11 to his or her premises for the purposes of examining and verifying the
inventories, records and application herein required.
   (b)   The filing of an application for a license, the contents of such
application, and the issuance of a license shall be confidential information
and no disclosure thereof shall be made, except such as may be necessary in the
administration of the provisions of this chapter, provided, however, that any
disclosure may be made with the consent of the applicant.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.04 BOND REQUIRED; CLAIMS AGAINST LICENSEE.
   Every applicant for the license required in §
818.02 shall execute and file with the City Manager a good and sufficient bond
in the sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000) with two or more sureties thereon
who shall be freeholders within the City, or with the surety thereon a surety
company authorized to do business in the State. Such bond shall be subject to
the approval of the Director of Law, shall be conditioned upon faithful
observance of all the provisions of this chapter and shall also indemnify any
purchaser at the distress merchandise sale who suffers any loss by reason of
any misrepresentation in the sale. The bond shall continue in effect until the
expiration of 90 days following the termination of the sale on all claims
secured by the bond. The licensee shall notify the City Manager of any suit
filed as a result of the operations hereby licensed. Any purchaser claiming to
have been damaged by any misrepresentation in the distress merchandise sale may
maintain an action at law against the licensee making such misrepresentation,
and may join as party defendant the surety or sureties on the bond as herein
provided.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.05 LICENSE FEE.
   The fee for the license required in §
818.02 shall be twenty-five dollars ($25.00).
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.06 LICENSE ISSUANCE; CONDITIONS UPON ISSUANCE.
   When it appears to the City Manager that all of the statements contained in
the application referred to in §
818.03 are true and that the proposed sale is of the character represented
therein, that the application is in full compliance with the terms and
conditions of this chapter and that the required license fee has been paid and
the required bond filed, the City Manager shall issue the license required in §
818.02 to the applicant authorizing the applicant to advertise and conduct the
sale as described in the application, subject to the following conditions:
   (a)   The sale shall be held at the place named in the application and by
the particular licensee for a period of not more than 30 consecutive calendar
days. However, the City Manager may waive the restrictions on distress
merchandise sales in cases where substantial physical damage has been incurred
to the applicant’s present inventory of merchandise.
   (b)   Only the goods, wares and merchandise included in the inventory
attached to the application shall be sold at the sale. Upon the commencement of
the sale and for its duration, the license issued shall be prominently
displayed in the place of sale by the licensee.
   (c)   The licensee shall keep accurate records during the sale at the
location in which the sale is conducted, which records shall be open to
examination by the City Manager or his or her examiners. Such records shall
indicate the amount of retail sales, the cost of goods on back order received
and other information relative to the sale that may be reasonably required by
the City Manager.
(Ord. O76-191, passed 10-19-1976)
§ 818.07 RESTRICTIONS UPON ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   (a)   The license required in §
818.02 shall not be issued for the sale of stock on hand of any person except a
bona fide merchant of the City and shall not be granted to any person who sets
up an establishment solely or principally for the purpose of conducting a
distress merchandise sale.
   (b)   Such license shall not be issued to any person who has been convicted
of violating any of the provisions of this chapter and no such person shall act
as an auctioneer or be employed in any manner at or in connection with any
licensed distress merchandise sale for a period of five years after such
conviction.
   (c)   Such license shall not be issued to any person for a period of two
years after the termination of a distress merchandise sale conducted by such
person under the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. O76-191, passed 10-19-1976)
§ 818.08 EFFECTIVE PERIOD OF LICENSE; EXTENSION.
   (a)   No distress merchandise sale shall be licensed for a period of more
than 30 consecutive calendar days.
(Ord. O76-191, passed 10-19-1976)
   (b)   The City Manager may, upon application therefor five days prior to the
thirtieth day of the distress merchandise sale, extend the period of the sale
for no longer than 15 consecutive calendar days, provided that he or she finds
from the records of the sale that more than 60% of the goods, wares and
merchandise included in the inventory remains unsold. The City Manager may,
upon application therefor five days prior to the forty-fifth day of the sale,
extend the period of the sale for no longer than 15 consecutive days, provided
that he or she finds from the records of the sale that more than 30% of the
goods, wares and merchandise included in the inventory remains unsold.
Thereafter, upon application therefor three days before the expiration of the
sixtieth day, the City Manager may extend such sale for no longer than 30 days
if it appears that there is merchandise included in the inventory remaining
unsold, provided, however, that such final extension shall be made only if he
or she finds 30% of the goods, wares and merchandise included in the inventory
remains unsold, and that every reasonable and bona fide effort has been made to
promote and complete the sale.
(Ord. 3708, passed 5-10-1961)
§ 818.09 LICENSE REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION.
   The City Manager, upon the recommendation of the examiners appointed
pursuant to §
818.11, or upon his or her own initiative, may at any time revoke or suspend
the license granted under authority of this chapter if any licensee offers for
sale any goods, wares or merchandise in addition to those permitted under this
chapter, or violates or fails to comply with any of the requirements or
provisions of this chapter, or any law relating to the business so licensed.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.10 APPEALS.
   In the case of the refusal to issue the license required in §
818.02, or the revocation or suspension of such license by the City Manager,
the applicant or licensee may appeal from such order to a Board of Appeals
composed of three members annually appointed by the City Council. Notice of
such appeal shall be filed in writing with the City Manager within ten days
after the making of such order. The Board of Appeals, within ten days after the
filing with the City Manager of such notice of appeal, shall proceed with the
hearing of such appeal, at which hearing all parties interested shall be
afforded an opportunity to be heard, and such Board of Appeals shall approve,
modify or annul such order from which the appeal has been perfected. The
finding of such Board of Appeals shall be final with respect to all interested
parties.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.11 APPOINTMENT OF EXAMINERS; POWERS AND DUTIES; BOND.
   The City Manager may, at his or her discretion, appoint qualified persons
for the examination and verification of the inventories, records and
applications provided for under this chapter. All information obtained by such
persons or any City employee or official shall be confidential. The examiners
appointed under this section may enter on the premises of any applicant and
make the necessary examinations and verifications of the inventories, records
and applications required under this chapter. The examiners shall be bonded in
the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) each by the City for the
truthful performance of their duties.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.12 PROMULGATION OF REGULATIONS.
   The City Manager is hereby authorized to promulgate regulations not
inconsistent with the purpose and intent of this chapter as he or she may from
time to time deem necessary or desirable, provided, however, that any such
regulations, before becoming effective, shall first be published at least once
in a local newspaper of general circulation.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.13 HOURS OF SALE.
   No person licensed under §
818.02 shall hold the distress merchandise sale or shall be open for business
at times other than the regular store hours of such person, except that the
City Manager in granting such license may provide for extra evening hours if
requested by the applicant, and if such request is reasonable.
(Ord. O76-191, passed 10-19-1976)
§ 818.14 COMMINGLING OF MERCHANDISE.
   (a)   The license required in §
818.02 shall be valid only for the sale of goods inventoried pursuant to §
818.03(e). The commingling of additional merchandise with inventoried
merchandise shall cause the inventoried merchandise to lose its identity as
distressed goods, and any such license issued shall cease to apply to the sale
of such goods.
   (b)   No person licensed under §
818.02 shall add any goods to the inventoried stock, except as provided in §
818.15 and no such person shall in the course of a distress merchandise sale
sell goods except those included in the original inventory, plus any addition
provided for in §
818.15. Each sale of goods not so inventoried shall constitute a separate
offense under this chapter.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.15 ADDITIONS TO INVENTORIED MERCHANDISE.
   No person licensed under §
818.02 shall in the course of a distress merchandise sale make any addition
whatsoever to the stock of merchandise set forth in the inventory attached to
the application for the license pursuant to §
818.03(e), except that such person is permitted to add new stock not to exceed
25% of the dollar value of the inventoried merchandise, for the purpose of
maintaining reasonably balanced selections. Such addition may be made only once
and must be reported to the City Manager’s office before being offered for
sale. Nothing shall be offered for sale or sold at any such distress
merchandise sale which is in excess of the original inventory as filed, plus
such permitted addition. Any abnormal purchase of merchandise by the applicant
prior to the application for the license required in §
818.02 shall be cause for refusal to issue the license. The examiners appointed
by the City Manager pursuant to §
818.11 may, as in the instance of the original inventory, verify this addition
to the inventory.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.16 MISREPRESENTATIONS.
   No person licensed under §
818.02 or his agent shall make any statement that is false in any particular or
that has a tendency to mislead, or shall make any misrepresentation whatsoever
with reference to any article sold or offered for sale during such distress
merchandise sale.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.17 ATTENDANCE OF LICENSEE.
   No person to whom the license required in §
818.02 has been issued or his or her authorized representative shall fail to
remain in continuous attendance at all times while the distress merchandise
sale is being conducted. Such person shall be responsible for the violation of
any of the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.18 EXEMPTION.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any sale conducted by a
public officer as part of his or her official duties or to any sale, an
accounting of which must be made to a court of law, or to any sale conducted
pursuant to an order of a court of law.
(Ord. 3652, passed 11-30-1960)
§ 818.99 PENALTY.
Editor’s note:
   See §
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.

   Police Division- see ADM.

§ 819.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   ALARM BUSINESS. The business by any individual, partnership,
corporation or other entity of: selling, leasing, maintaining, servicing,
repairing, altering, replacing, moving or installing any alarm system or
causing to be sold, leased, maintained, serviced, repaired, altered, replaced,
moved or installed any alarm system in or on any building, structure or
facility.
   (b)   ALARM SYSTEM. Any mechanical or electrical device which is designed or
used for the detection of an unauthorized entry into a building, structure or
facility or for alerting others of the commission of an unlawful act within a
building, structure or facility, or both; or for the detection of fire, which
emits a sound or transmits a signal or message when actuated. Alarm systems
include, but are not limited to, direct dial telephone devices, audible alarms
and proprietor alarms. Devices which are not designed or used to register
alarms that are audible, visible or perceptible outside of the protected
building, structure or facility are not included within this definition.
   (c)   FALSE ALARM. An alarm signal necessitating a response by the Police
Division or the Fire Division where there is no physical sign that an emergency
existed. However, an alarm is not false if the owner thereof, after such alarm
has  emitted a signal, notifies the Police Division or the Fire Division, as
the case may be, that the signal was accidental, and if such notification
occurs prior to the dispatching of police or fire officers to the location of
the alarm.
(Ord. O84-33, passed 4-3-1984)
§ 819.02 EQUIPMENT REGULATION.
   (a)   All equipment used in installations for which a permit is required
under this chapter shall meet the applicable standards of Underwriters’
Laboratories, Inc., and/or the National Fire Protection Association, and/or
other recognized industry standards. An applicant may be required to submit
evidence of the reliability and suitability of the equipment to be installed.
   (b)   All equipment, the use or installation of which is subject to this
chapter, shall be maintained in good operating condition. The Chief of Police
and/or the Chief of Fire may require that repairs be made whenever he or she
has determined that such are necessary to assure proper operation.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.03 PERMITS REQUIRED.
   (a)   Alarm business. No person shall engage in, conduct or carry on an
alarm business within the City without first applying for and receiving an
alarm business permit therefor in accordance with the provisions of this
chapter.
   (b)   Alarm system. No person shall possess or use an alarm system without
first applying for and receiving an alarm permit therefor in accordance with
the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.04 ISSUANCE OF PERMITS.
   The issuing and approving authority shall be the Chief of Police of the
City.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.05 APPLICATION FORMS.
   Applications for all permits required under this chapter shall be filed with
the Chief of Police and shall be accompanied by the requisite fee. The Chief of
Police shall prescribe the form of the application and request such information
as is necessary to evaluate and act upon the application.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.06 APPLICATION, INVESTIGATION AND DENIAL.
   (a)   Alarm business. Every application for an alarm business shall require
the name of the proprietor of the business; the names of the partners of the
business if it is a partnership; the names of the officers and principal
stockholders if it is a corporation; and the names of every employee of the
business who will engage in the business of installing, repairing, servicing,
selling, leasing or maintaining an alarm system. The Chief of Police shall
conduct an appropriate investigation of the applicant to determine whether such
permit shall be issued. The Police Chief may require additional information of
applicants which he or she deems necessary to conduct his or her investigation.
The permit shall be denied by the Chief of Police if:
      (1)   The character or reputation of the applicant, its partners,
officers, stockholders or employees is determined to be inimical to the safety
or general welfare of the community;
      (2)   The applicant does not comply with the standards and regulations
adopted pursuant to this chapter; or
      (3)   The applicant, his or her employee or agent has knowingly made any
false, misleading or fraudulent statement of a material fact in the application
for a permit.
   (b)   Alarm system. The permit shall be denied by the Police Chief if the
alarm system does not comply with standards and regulations adopted pursuant to
this chapter. Such permit shall be issued to the person owning, using or
possessing the alarm system.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.07 APPEAL PROCEDURE.
   An applicant denied a permit may appeal within 15 days of such denial to the
City Manager who shall hold a hearing thereon or appoint a hearing officer to
hold a hearing thereon, within 15 days from receipt of the notice of appeal.
The City Manager or his or her hearing officer may affirm or reverse the denial
of the permit.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.08 FEE FOR ALARM BUSINESS PERMITS.
   An annual permit fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) shall be due and
payable on February 1, 1978, and on February 1 of each subsequent year, for
each alarm business doing business within the City. Such permit fee shall not
be prorated.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.09 FEE FOR ALARM SYSTEM PERMITS; RENEWALS.
   The fee for an alarm system permit shall be ten dollars ($10.00) for type A-
B residences and twenty dollars ($20.00) for type C-D residences and shall not
be prorated. February 1 shall be the anniversary date for all such permits.
Such permits issued on February 1 shall expire three years after such issuance.
Such permits issued subsequent to any February 1 shall expire three years after
such February 1. Applications for the renewal of permits shall be processed in
the same manner as applications for the initial permit. The fee for a renewal
of a permit shall be ten dollars ($10.00) for type A-B residences and twenty
dollars ($20.00) for type C-D residences for each successive three-year period.
§ 819.10 AUTOMATIC DIALING DEVICES.
   (a)   The City may subscribe to one or more telephone lines for burglar or
robbery alarms, or for fire alarm purposes, or for similar purposes, and when
any line is so designated as provided for herein, persons may, upon proper
application and compliance with applicable laws, be granted a permit to install
a device or devices which automatically select the designated telephone line
for the purpose of playing a recorded message or to otherwise report an
intrusion or other emergency.
   (b)   No person shall use or cause to be used, for burglar or robbery or
fire alarm purposes, any telephone device or telephone attachment that
automatically selects any telephone line allocated by the telephone company to
the City or any of its departments or divisions, except a telephone line which
may be specifically designated by the City Manager for such purpose. Such
designated telephone line or lines shall terminate at the police station or
fire station communications centers.
   (c)   For alarms of the type described herein, the message shall comply with
the following restrictions:
      (1)   The length of the message shall not exceed 15 seconds.
      (2)   The message shall not be repeated more than three times for each
dialing.
      (3)   The message shall first state: “This is a recording.” The balance
of the message shall be appropriate to the purpose for which the alarm is
installed and shall be subject to the approval of the Chief of Police and/or
the Chief of Fire. The entire message shall be intelligible.
   (d)   For alarms of the type herein described, each such device shall be
programmed to first dial the police station or fire station, using an unlisted
number assigned for that purpose. The device shall next dial a number selected
by the applicant, such second number being that at which a person having a key
to the building where the alarm is installed can normally be found. A third
number subject to the approval of the Chief of Police or the Chief of Fire may
be programmed for the next dialing. Not more than three such dialings may be
programmed except under unusual circumstances and upon approval by the Chief of
Police or the Chief of Fire. No enforcement agency other than the City Division
of Police or Division of Fire may be selected.
   (e)   The cost of providing the service described above, including any fee
or payment charged by the telephone company, shall be paid by the applicant.
   (f)   The fee to be charged by the City shall be determined on an annual
basis by dividing the cost of phone service for such purpose to the City by the
number of holders of permits for alarms, adding 15% for administration and
rounding off to the next highest dollar, except that the minimum charge shall
be twenty dollars ($20.00) per year per subscriber. All fees shall be payable
on a calendar year basis in advance. Delinquency in excess of ten days shall
result in cancellation of the permit or permits.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.11 ALARMS CONNECTED DIRECTLY TO POLICE STATION.
   (a)   Upon proper application by any alarm system permittee to connect to
the police emergency alarm board to receive emergency alarms, the Chief of
Police may issue a permit or permits for such connection.
   (b)   For use of an alarm terminal supplied by the City, the applicant shall
pay to the City the sum of sixty-five dollars ($65.00) and, in addition, shall
pay a fee of twenty dollars ($20.00) per year for the monitoring of the same.
   (c)   Each alarm system permittee connected to such system shall be
responsible for the maintenance and operation of his or her respective signal
line.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.12 GROUNDS FOR SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION OF PERMITS.
   The following shall constitute grounds for suspension and revocation of
permits:
   (a)   The violation of any provision of this chapter;
   (b)   The failure to comply with standards or regulations adopted pursuant
to this chapter;
   (c)   Where any alarm business permittee, his or her agent or employee is
charged with a crime involving moral turpitude or where the character,
reputation or moral integrity of the permit holder or his or her employees is
determined to be inimical to public safety or the general welfare of the
community;
   (d)   Where an alarm system actuates excessive false alarms, in the
reasonable opinion of the Chief of Police or Chief of Fire, except that no
suspension or revocation may be made under this division unless the permittee
has been issued a letter of warning by the Chief of Police or Chief of Fire and
has been given a reasonable period of time to take corrective action;
   (e)   Where the applicant or permittee, his or her employee or agent has
knowingly made any false, misleading or fraudulent statement of a material fact
in the application for a permit; or
   (f)   Where a twenty-five dollar ($25.00) civil penalty has been assessed by
the Chief of Police under § 819.121 and the permittee has failed to pay such
civil penalty within 15 days.
(Ord. O84-33, passed 4-3-1984)
§ 819.125 CIVIL PENALTY FOR FALSE ALARMS.
   A civil penalty of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) is hereby assessed against
an alarm permittee whose alarm emits more than three false alarms in any one
calendar year and for each false alarm thereafter.
(Ord. O84-33, passed 4-3-1984)
§ 819.13 SUSPENDING AND REVOKING AUTHORITY.
   Any permit issued under this chapter may be suspended by the Chief of Police
for the grounds listed in §
819.12.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.14 PROCEDURE.
   (a)   The determination of the Police Chief with regard to matters of
suspension shall be appealable in the time and manner set forth in §
819.07. The Police Chief, in the case of such suspension, shall serve the
permittee with a written order of suspension, which shall state the reasons for
such suspension. The order shall be effective immediately if personally served,
or 48 hours after the same has been deposited in the course of transmission in
the United States Postal Service.
   (b)   Immediately upon such an order becoming effective, the permittee shall
discontinue the use of any alarm system requiring a permit under this chapter
and cease all operations conducted under the authority of any permit issued
pursuant to this chapter.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.15 REVOCATION OF PERMITS.
   The suspension shall become a revocation 15 days after the order of
suspension becomes effective unless the permittee files an appeal of the order
of suspension in the manner set forth in §
819.07. Where an appeal is filed, the order of suspension shall be stayed
pending a determination thereon by the City Manager or a hearing officer
appointed by the City Manager. Such suspension shall become a revocation if the
decision of the City Manager or his or her hearing officer upholds the
suspension. The suspension shall be dissolved immediately if the decision of
the City Manager or his or her hearing officer reverses the suspension.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.16 SURRENDER OF PERMIT.
   If a permit is revoked pursuant to this chapter, the permittee shall
surrender such permit to the Chief of Police.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.17 EXCEPTION.
   A financial institution required by State or Federal law or regulation to
maintain an alarm system shall be exempt from the suspension and revocation
sections of this chapter but shall be subject to the penalties provided for
violations of this chapter.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.18 DISPOSITION OF FEES.
   All moneys derived from fees paid pursuant to the provisions of this chapter
shall be deposited to the credit of the General Fund of the City.
(Ord. O77-221, passed 1-3-1978)
§ 819.99 PENALTY.
Editor’s note:
   See §
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.
