§ 1420.01 NATIONAL ELECTRIC CODE ADOPTED.
   Pursuant to
Article IV, § 6 of the City Charter, there is hereby adopted by and for the
City the current edition of the National Electrical Code, as adopted by the
State of Ohio, designated NFPA No. 70, and sponsored by the National Fire
Protection Association, save and except such portions as are hereinafter
amended or deleted.
(Ord. 2002-6, passed 2-5-2002; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004; Am. Ord.
O2005-56, passed 7-5- 2005; Am. Ord. O2007-51, passed 7-3-2007; Am. Ord. O2008-
20, passed 3-4-2008; Am. Ord. O2008- 37, passed 4-15-2008; Am. Ord. O2018-34,
passed 11-20-2018)
§ 1420.02 FILE AND DISTRIBUTION COPIES.
   At least one copy of the National Electrical Code, as adopted in §
1420.01, shall be on file in the office of the Clerk of the City Council for
inspection by the public.
(Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004)
§ 1420.03 CONFLICT OF LAWS.
   In the event of a conflict between any of the provisions of the National
Electrical Code, as adopted in §
1420.01, and any provision of this Part Fourteen - Building and Housing Code,
or any other provision of these Codified Ordinances, or any other local
ordinance, the local provision shall prevail.
§ 1420.04 ENFORCEMENT.
   (a)   Superintendent of Inspection for the City shall enforce the provisions
of this chapter
   (b)   Should there be any change in interpretation of the provisions of the
National Electrical Code, as adopted in §
1420.01, by any official of the City with power to so interpret, such change
shall be transmitted to all Master A licensees at least 30 days before such
interpretation becomes effective.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1420.05 AMENDMENTS.
   The National Electrical Code, as adopted in §
1420.01, is hereby amended as follows: 210-52(c) Counter tops: (Amended) In
kitchens and dining rooms of dwelling units, receptacle outlets for counter
spaces shall be installed in accordance with (1) through (5) below.
   (1)   Wall counter spaces. A receptacle outlet shall be installed at each
wall counter space 12 inches (305 mm) or wider. Receptacle outlets shall be
installed so that no point along the wall line is more than 24 inches (610 mm),
measured horizontally from a receptacle outlet in that space.
   (2)   Island counter spaces. (Optional) at least one receptacle outlet shall
be installed at each island counter space with a long dimension of 24 inches
(610 mm) or greater and a short dimension of 12 inches (305 mm) or greater.
   (3)   Peninsular counter spaces. (Optional) at least one receptacle outlet
shall be installed at each peninsular counter space with a long dimension of 24
inches (610 mm) or greater and a short dimension of 12 inches (305 mm) or
greater.
   (4)   Separate spaces. Countertop spaces separated by range tops,
refrigerators, or sinks shall be considered as separate countertop spaces in
applying the requirements of (2) and (3) above.
   (5)   Receptacle outlet location. Receptacle outlets shall be located not
more than 18 inches (458 mm) above the countertop. Receptacle outlets shall not
be installed in a face-up position in the work surfaces or countertops.
Receptacle outlets rendered not readily accessible by appliances fastened in
place or appliances occupying dedicated space shall not be considered as these
required outlets. Exception: where acceptable to the authority having
jurisdiction and to meet the special conditions as specified in (a) or (b)
below, receptacle outlets shall be permitted to be mounted not more than 12
inches (305 mm) below the countertops. Receptacles mounted below the countertop
in accordance with this exception shall not be located where the countertop
extends more than 6 inches (153 mm) beyond its support base.
      (a)   Construction for the physically impaired.
      (b)   Where island or peninsular counter space construction precludes
practical mounting above the countertop.
(Ord. O98-12, passed 2-3-1998)
§ 1420.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions and
requirements of the National Electrical Code, as adopted in §
1420.01, or fails to comply with any order made thereunder, or violates any
detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved
thereunder, is guilty, severally for each and every such violation and
noncompliance respectively, of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more
than one hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed
committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or
continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or the
application of any other equitable remedy.

§ 1422.01 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR WORK. Means and includes the work of installing
wires, conduits, apparatus, fixtures and other appliances for carrying or using
electricity for light, heat or power purposes.
   (b)   MASTER ELECTRICIAN. A person registered as a master electrician with
the City. In order to register as a master electrician the person must possess
an active license issued by the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board in
accordance with Ohio R.C. Chapter 4740 for an electrical contractor as that
term is defined in Ohio R.C. 4740.01(B), (hereinafter a State license). Only a
master electrician may apply for permits and be the representative of the
business entity in all matters relating to Title Six of Part Fourteen of the
Codified Ordinances.
   (c)   ELECTRICAL JOURNEYMAN. A person registered as an electrical journeyman
with the City, and performing the actual physical electrical contractor’s work.
An electrical journeyman must be working under the general direction and
supervision of a master electrician registered to work in the City. Electrical
journeyman contractors cannot obtain permits.
   (d)   ELECTRICAL APPRENTICE. A person, registered as an electrical
apprentice with the City, who is employed by a master electrician registered to
work in the City and in the process of learning the electrical trade by
practical experience, under the instruction and direct supervision of a master
electrician or electrical journeyman.
(Ord. 3766, passed 12-13-1961; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010 )
§ 1422.02 LICENSE AND REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   No person shall act as a master electrician, electrical journeyman or
electrical apprentice in the City without first registering with the City in
accordance with this chapter.
   (b)   No more than three electrical apprentices shall be engaged in any work
for each master electrician or electrical journeyman actually present on the
job.
   (c)   Any business entity engaged in electrical contractor work must have as
a principal or in its employ a person possessing an active State license and
registered with the City as a master electrician. Such person shall apply for
all permits and shall be the representative of the business entity in all
matters relating to Title Six of Part Fourteen of the Codified Ordinances. If
such person should terminate or sever their relationship with the business
entity, such entity must cease all electrical work unless and until another
principal or employee has obtained a registration as a master electrician from
the City.
(Ord. 3766, passed 12-13-1961; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.03 REGISTRATION APPLICATION AND FEES.
   (a)   The fee for registration of a master electrician shall be two hundred
dollars ($200.00) to be paid at the time of registration. Every person upon
registration shall present a copy of their active State license to the City
along with evidence that they are insured in the minimum amount as required by
the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board in accordance with Ohio R.C.
4740.06(B)(4). The active state license must name the same company as that
listed on the registration application. The proof of insurance shall name the
City of Middletown as the certificate holder. The master registration shall
specify the name of the person so registered, who shall thereby be authorized
to engage in the occupation of a master electrician.
   (b)   An electrical journeyman registration shall be issued to any person
who has duly made application therefore and has passed the examination with a
minimum score of 70% as prescribed by the City. Persons desiring to take the
examination for an electrical journeyman registration shall make written
application therefore, accompanied by a fee of fifty dollars ($50.00). Such
fees shall not be refunded, but any applicant failing the examination shall be
entitled to one re-examination without fee. Exams must be completed within 90
days of the application date. The electrical journeyman registration shall
specify the name of the person so registered, who shall thereby be authorized
to perform work as an electrical journeyman.
   (c)   An electrical apprentice registration shall be issued, without
examination, to beginners or electrical apprentices employed by a person
registered as a master electrician with the City, upon application and payment
of the fee of twenty dollars ($20.00). The electrical apprentice registration
shall specify the name of the person so registered, who shall thereby be
authorized to perform work as an electrical apprentice.
(Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-1981; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2009-93, passed 12-1-2009; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.04 EXPIRATION AND RENEWAL OF REGISTRATIONS.
   (a)   The registration of each master electrician shall expire on December
31 of each year, but may be renewed by the person holding the same upon
application and payment of the renewal fee of fifty dollars ($50.00). Every
master electrician, upon each renewal of registration, must present a copy of
their active State license and a copy of a certificate of liability insurance
verifying insurance in the minimum amount as required by the Ohio Construction
Industry Examining Board in accordance with Ohio R.C. 4740.06(B) and listing
the City of Middletown as the certificate holder. The application for renewal
and the fee shall be filed with the Chief Building Official each year on or
after November 1, but before January 1. If the registration has not been
renewed on or before December 31 it will expire. The holder of the registration
may renew the registration through January of the following year. Payment for
renewal must be received in the Building Inspection office by January 31. After
January 31, the master electrician must re-register in accordance with Section
1422.01(b) of this chapter.
   (b)   The registration of each electrical journeyman shall expire on
December 31 of each year, but may be renewed, without examination, upon payment
of the renewal fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00). The fee shall be paid to
the Chief Building Official each year on or after November 1, but before
January 1. If the registration has not been renewed on or before December 31 it
will expire. The holder of the registration may renew the registration through
January of the following year. Payment for renewal must be received in the
Building Inspection office by January 31. After January 31 the electrical
journeyman must re-register in accordance with Section 1422.01(c) of this
chapter, including all testing requirements.
   (c)   The registration of each electrical apprentice shall expire on
December 31 of each year but may be renewed upon payment of the renewal fee of
ten dollars ($10.00). The fee shall be paid to the Chief Building Official each
year on or after November 1, but before January 1. If the registration has not
been renewed on or before December 31 it will expire. The holder of the
registration may renew the registration through January of the following year.
Payment for renewal must be received in the Building Inspection office by
January 31. After January 31 the electrical apprentice must re-register be in
accordance with Section 1422.01(d) of this chapter.
(Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-1981; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.05 TRANSFERABILITY.
   The registrations required by this chapter shall not be transferable.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.06 RECIPROCITY WITH OTHER MUNICIPALITIES.
   (a)   Any person registered as an electrical journeyman by any other
municipal corporation of the State, upon payment of the prescribed fee shall be
issued an electrical journeyman registration without examination.
   (b)   The provisions of this section shall not apply to registrants of
municipal corporations that do not waive similar requirements for registrants
of the City, nor shall they apply to an applicant for a registration who is
unable to provide satisfactory proof, as may be required by the City, that such
applicant is qualified to perform the contemplated work.
(Ord. 3453, passed 3-25-1959; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.07 REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF REGISTRATION.
   (a)   The Chief Building Official may review the registration of any
electrical journeyman or electrical apprentice under this chapter to determine
whether it should be revoked, be suspended or not be renewed; or that a
registration requested under this chapter not be issued to an applicant, if the
registrant or applicant has done any of the following:
      (1)   Been convicted of a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or a
felony;
      (2)   Violated any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules adopted
pursuant to it;
      (3)   Obtained the registration by means of fraud or misrepresentation;
or
      (4)   Been guilty of gross misconduct in pursuit of their profession.
   (b)   Upon becoming aware of circumstances or facts which suggest that the
registrant or applicant has done any of the acts listed in divisions (a)(1)
through (a)(4) of this section, the Chief Building Official shall investigate
such facts or circumstances. If, after such investigation, the Chief Building
Official finds that there is probable cause to believe an act listed in
divisions (a)(1) through (a)(4) of this section has been committed by a
registrant or applicant, the Chief Building Official shall request that the
Board of Appeals review the registration or application for registration to
determine if the same should be revoked, suspended or not renewed, or whether
the application for registration should be denied. Notice of such request for
review shall be sent by ordinary mail delivery to the registrant or applicant
at the last address supplied by them. The notice shall include that a review
has been requested and a general statement of the grounds for proposed action.
The Board of Appeals shall conduct a review of the issues relating to the
registration or application in accordance with Chapter 1460 of this Title.
   (c)   (1)   If after review, the Board of Appeals determines that grounds
exist for action to be taken regarding the registration or application, the
Board of Appeals may:
         A.   Revoke the registration; or
         B.   Suspend the registration; or
         C.   Refuse to issue or renew the registration.
      (2)   If the registration is revoked, the Board of Appeals shall
determine if the registrant may apply for reinstatement, and if so, when. The
Board of Appeals may require examination for reinstatement of a registration
issued by the City for electrical journeymen.
   (d)   Nothing in this section is intended to limit the right of the City to
seek legal redress for violation of this chapter or any rules promulgated in
accordance with it.
   (e)   Upon becoming aware of circumstances or facts, which suggest that a
master electrician has done any of the acts listed in divisions (a)(1) through
(a)(4) of this section, the Chief Building Official shall report such
information to the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board for their review
and action.
(Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.08 DISPLAY OF REGISTRATION AND REGISTRATION CARD.
   Holders of a master electrician registration shall keep said registration
displayed in a conspicuous place in their principal office or place of
business. All persons holding a master electrician, electrical journeyman or
electrical apprentice registration shall carry the registration card with them
when on the job site.
(Ord. 3766, passed 12-13-1961; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.09 DISPLAY OF NAME AND LICENSE NUMBER.
   All persons holding a master electrician registration shall identify all
business vehicles with the name of the registration holder, and with the number
of their state license, in letters/numerals not less than two inches high on
the exterior of the vehicle.
(Ord. O95-112, passed 10-3-1995; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.10 UNREGISTERED PERSONNEL ON JOB SITE.
   No registered master electrician shall permit any person employed by or
working for said master electrician, including subcontractors, to be working at
the job site unless registered with the City according to the provisions of
this chapter.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.11 EXEMPTIONS.
   (a)   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any of the
following:
      (1)   Work in connection with the erection, construction, maintenance or
repair of lines for the transmission of electricity from the source of supply
to the service, or on the premises used by electric light plants authorized to
generate and sell electrical current;
      (2)   Electric street railway companies or the work of such companies on
premises owned or controlled by them;
      (3)   The work of electric light plants in installing, maintaining and
repairing on the premises of customers, service connections and meters and
other apparatus remaining the property of such plants or companies after
installation;
      (4)   Work in connection with the lighting of public streets, alleys or
public parks and bridges; or
      (5)   The work of telephone and telegraph companies incorporated for the
transmission of intelligence by electricity or the installing, maintaining or
repairing of wires, apparatus, fixtures or other appliances used by such
companies that are necessary for or incident to their business, whether or not
such wires, conduits, apparatus, fixtures or other appliances are on their own
premises.
   (b)   Electricians employed by theatrical companies may install temporary
wiring and appliances required for the purpose of the engagement of any such
company, subject to the supervision of a person licensed under this chapter.
   (c)   Electricians regularly employed as maintenance electricians by firms
or corporations, other than the holders of a State license, may install such
electrical wiring, conduits and appliances or make such repairs thereon as may
be required without any certificate obtained under this chapter but only on the
premises of such firms or corporations. If such electricians desire to install
any electrical wires, conduits or appliances or make any repairs thereon not on
the premises of the firms or corporations by which they are regularly employed,
they shall first apply for and take the examination required by this chapter
and become licensed in accordance with the terms of this chapter.
   (d)   This chapter shall not apply to departments, branches, service units
or buildings of the Federal or State government.
   (e)   A registration under the provisions of this chapter is not required of
the owner-occupant of a single-family dwelling who performs the work governed
by this Title Six as to such dwelling, provided that such person obtains the
permits required in Chapter 1424 and submits such work for the inspections
required.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1422.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the City from ordering that work being performed be
stopped pending compliance with State and local laws, the enforced removal of
prohibited conditions or the application of any other equitable remedy.
(Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)

§ 1424.01 SCOPE OF CHAPTER.
   The provisions of this chapter shall apply to the erection or construction
of new wiring attached to any building or structure, including all overhead or
underground wiring systems through or by which is conveyed, or intended to be
conveyed, electric current for any purpose whatever, and the maintenance in
good and safe condition of such system and the making of the necessary repairs
and changes.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1424.02 INSPECTION REQUIRED.
   (a)   Every electrical installation provided for in §
1424.01 shall be subject to inspection and approval by an engineering expert,
bureau or board designated as an inspection agency duly authorized by the City
Council to make such inspection and approval. Any such expert, bureau, board or
inspection agency shall be under the supervision and control of the
Superintendent of Inspection.
   (b)   The electrical contractor shall notify the Superintendent at such time
as any work is to be commenced. If the Superintendent requires plans for such
work, these shall be submitted in duplicate if the same are not already on file
as a part of the original building plans of the improvement. A permit for such
work shall be obtained at that time. If plans are not required by the
Superintendent, work may be commenced and a permit acquired at any time prior
to rough-in installation. Inspection fees shall be paid at the time a permit is
obtained.
   (c)   When the installation has been satisfactorily completed, the inspector
shall issue a certificate of approval, a copy of which shall be transmitted to
the Superintendent.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1424.03 PROCEDURE AS TO DEFECTIVE WORK.
   If the person inspecting pursuant to §
1424.02 finds a defect in any work, he or she shall notify the contractor in
writing to remedy such defect within a reasonable stated number of days. A copy
of such notification shall be sent to the Superintendent of Inspection. At the
end of the specified period the Superintendent shall determine if correction
has been made and if not so made, he or she shall file the necessary action
under the provisions of Chapter 1420.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1424.04 SPECIAL SUPERVISION.
   (a)   Where the work covered by the plans required in §
1424.02 involves construction or building service equipment that is hazardous
or complex, or for other good reason requires special or expert supervision,
the architect who signed such plans or the professional engineer who affixed
his or her seal thereto or made the plans or computations for such work shall
supervise the work and be responsible for its conformity with the plans as they
relate to safety and sanitation. Where the architect or professional engineer
is not available, another architect, professional engineer or other qualified
person shall perform the required supervision.
   (b)   Where such special supervision has been performed, the person
performing it shall make and file with the Superintendent of Inspection a
certificate that he or she has done so and that the completed work conforms
with the plans. Such certificate may be in lieu of inspection by the
Superintendent, provided that this section shall not be construed to deprive
the Superintendent of jurisdiction over the inspection of the work or to
prohibit him or her from making inspection, should he feel that such inspection
is necessary to assure compliance with the plans.
(Ord. 4214, passed 7-6-1965)
§ 1424.05 ANNUAL PERMIT; FEES.
   (a)   Annual approval. In lieu of an individual approval for each alteration
to an existing electrical, gas mechanical or plumbing installation, the
building official may issue an annual approval upon application therefore to
any person, firm or corporation regularly employing individuals holding the
appropriate inspector certificate from the Board of Building Standards of the
State of Ohio in the building, structure or on the premises owned or operated
by the applicant for the approval.
   (b)   Annual approval records. The person to whom an annual approval is
issued shall keep a detailed record of alterations made under such annual
approval. The building official shall have access to such records at all times
or such records shall be filed with the building official as designated. These
records shall include the applicable construction documents in accordance with
§ 106.1 of the Ohio Building Code and § 112 of the Ohio Residential Code.
   (c)   (1)   The fees for each annual approval shall be as follows:
 
Company employing certified plumbing inspector   $50.00
Company employing certified electrical inspector $50.00
Company employing certified mechanical inspector $50.00
 
      (2)   Such fees shall be paid into the City treasury by the
Superintendent after receipt thereof by him or her.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004)
§ 1424.06 ELECTRICAL PERMIT AND INSPECTION FEES.
   Fees for the issuance of a permit and the subsequent inspection of the work
performed under the permit are as follows:
   (a)   Residential.
      (1)   New construction:
         A.   Single-family: one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175.00) + seven
dollars ($7.00) per circuit over 15 circuits.
         B.   Multifamily: one hundred fifteen dollars ($115.00) per unit.
      (2)   Alterations or remodeling:
         A.   Interior alterations: eighty-five dollars ($85.00) base + seven
dollars ($7.00) per circuit.
         B.   Additions: eighty-five dollars ($85.00) base + seven dollars
($7.00) per circuit.
   (b)   Commercial and industrial:
      (1)   New construction:
         A.   Building: two hundred ten dollars ($210.00) base + seven dollars
($7.00) per circuit.
      (2)   Alterations or remodeling:
         A.   Interior alterations: one hundred fifteen dollars ($115.00) +
seven dollars ($7.00) per circuit.
         B.   Additions: one hundred and forty-five dollars ($145.00) base +
seven dollars ($7.00) per circuit added.
   (c)   Miscellaneous Single Inspections: Such as, but not limited to:
construction poles, service changes, signs, temporary service: eighty-five
dollars ($85.00).
   (d)   Wiring for HVAC Replacement: eighty-five dollars ($85.00).
   (e)   All Reinspections: sixty dollars ($60.00).
(Ord. O94-87, passed 6-21-1994; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004; Am. Ord.
O2011-54, passed 11-15-2011; Am. Ord. O2018-34, passed 11-20-2018)
§ 1424.07 EXEMPTIONS.
   All work covered by this Title shall be inspected by the Chief Building
Official except the following:
   (a)   Electric bells, gas lighting apparatus, call bells, burglar alarms,
telephones, telegraphs, district messengers, and similar installations; the
Chief Building Official may require such changes as he deems necessary in any
such system, however, when it becomes crossed or is likely to become crossed
with any lighting, heating or power system.
   (b)   Minor repairs such as the repairing of flush and snap switches,
replacing of fuses, changing lamp sockets and receptacles, taping joints and
repairing drop cords, replacement of lamps or the connection of portable
devices to suitable receptacles that have been permanently installed;
   (c)   The installation of wiring, devices or equipment for the operation of
signals or communications systems owned by telephone or telegraph companies;
   (d)   The installation of electric wiring, devices or equipment installed by
a public utility operating under a franchise, for installation or repair of its
own lines; and
   (e)   Any electrical work performed on or relating to equipment wiring as a
part of a manufacturing process in a manufacturing plant.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004)
§ 1424.08 CONCEALED WORK.
   No concealed wiring shall be lathed over or in any manner be concealed from
sight until inspected or approved by the Superintendent of Inspection.
(Ord. 3231, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1424.09 WAIVER OF CERTAIN FEES.
   Fees shall be waived for any building or structure or portion thereof
erected by the State or any agency thereof, or by any political subdivision of
the State or any agency of any such political subdivision, and also for any
building, except that fees for one, two and three-family dwellings shall not be
waived. Such waiver of fees shall not be deemed a waiver of plan review and
permit requirements.
(Ord. O83-34, passed 4-5-1983; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004)
§ 1424.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or the
application of any other equitable remedy.

§ 1426.01 OHIO PLUMBING CODE ADOPTED.
   Pursuant to
Article IV, § 6, of the City Charter, there is hereby adopted by and for the
City, for the purpose of establishing minimum standards for performing the work
therein concerned for all buildings, that certain code known as the Ohio
Plumbing Code, current edition as adopted by the State of Ohio, consisting of
Chapter 4101:3 of the Ohio Administrative Code.
(Ord. O98-75, passed 9-15-1998; Am. Ord. 2002-6, passed 2-5-2002; Am. Ord.

1426.01, shall be on file in the office of the Clerk of the City Council for
inspection by the public.
(Am. Ord. O2018-34, passed 11-20-2018)
§ 1426.03 CONFLICT OF LAWS.
   In the event of any conflict between the requirements of the Ohio Plumbing
Code, as adopted in §
1426.01, and those of any other code adopted by the City or any City ordinance,
the Ohio Plumbing Code shall prevail.

§ 1426.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions and
requirements of this chapter, or fails to comply with any order made
thereunder, or violates any detailed statement of specifications or plans
submitted and approved thereunder, shall, severally for each and every such
violation and noncompliance, respectively, be guilty of a minor misdemeanor and
shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense
shall be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation or
noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or the
application of any other equitable remedy.

§ 1428.01 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   PLUMBER’S WORK. Means and includes the work performed on all piping in
a building upon which tests are required to a point of three feet outside the
foundation walls and includes the house drain, soil, waste or vent stack,
conductors and roof leaders. Such work also includes the installation, repair
or replacement of water heaters or other plumbing fixtures. Such work further
includes the installation, repair or replacement of all water and sewer lines
outside the building to the property or curb line, or to a septic tank.
   (b)   MASTER PLUMBER. A person registered as a master plumber with the City.
In order to register as a master plumber the person must possess an active
license issued by the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board in accordance
with Ohio R.C. Chapter 4740 for a plumbing contractor, as that term is defined
in Ohio R.C. 4740.01(B)(hereinafter a State License). Only a master plumber may
apply for permits and be the representative of the business entity in all
matters relating to Title Eight of Part Fourteen of the Codified Ordinances.
   (c)   PLUMBING JOURNEYMAN. A person registered as a plumbing journeyman with
the City, and performing the actual physical plumbing contractor's work. A
plumbing journeyman must be working under the general direction and supervision
of a master plumber registered to work in the City. Plumbing journeyman
contractors cannot obtain permits.
   (d)   PLUMBING APPRENTICE. A person, registered as a plumbing apprentice
with the City, who is employed by a master plumber registered to work in the
City and in the process of learning the plumbing trade by practical experience,
under the instruction and direct supervision of a master plumber or plumbing
journeyman.
(Ord. 3265, passed 11-2-1957; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.02 LICENSE AND REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   No person shall act as a master plumber, plumbing journeyman, or
plumbing apprentice in the City without first registering with the City in
accordance with this chapter.
   (b)   No more than three plumbing apprentices shall be engaged in any work
for each master plumber or plumbing journeyman actually present on the job.
   (c)   Any business entity engaged in plumber’s work must have as a principal
or in its employ a person possessing an active State license and registered
with the City as a master plumber. Such person shall apply for all permits and
shall be the representative of the business entity in all matters relating to
Title Eight of Part Fourteen of the Codified Ordinances. If such person should
terminate or sever their relationship with the business entity, such entity
must cease all plumbing work unless and until another principal or employee has
obtained a registration as a master plumber from the City.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.03 REGISTRATION APPLICATION AND FEES.
   (a)   The fee for registration of a master plumber shall be two hundred
dollars ($200.00) to be paid at the time of registration. Every person, upon
registration, shall present a copy of their active State license to the City
along with evidence that they are insured in the minimum amount as required by
the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board in accordance with Ohio R.C.
4740.06(B)(4), and a bond approved by the Director of Law in the penal sum of
ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00). Such bond shall be conditioned to reimburse
the City for actual damages caused by act or omission of the plumber to any
property, and to hold the City free and harmless from all claims for damages
due to the negligence or misfeasance of such master plumber, or that may be
occasioned by reason of any opening made in any street, public land, alley or
avenue, in the making of any connection with any public or private sewer. Such
bond shall be in force from the date of its acceptance to the expiration date
listed on the bond and must be renewed annually. The active state license must
name the same company as that listed on the registration application. The proof
of insurance shall name the City of Middletown as the certificate holder. The
master plumber registration shall specify the name of the person so registered,
who shall thereby be authorized to engage in the occupation of a master
plumber.
   (b)   A plumbing journeyman registration shall be issued to any person who
has duly made application therefore and has passed the examination with a
minimum score of 70%, as prescribed by the City. Persons desiring to take the
examination for a plumbing journeyman registration shall make written
application therefor, accompanied by a fee of fifty dollars ($50.00). Such fees
shall not be refunded, but any applicant failing the examination shall be
entitled to one re-examination without fee. Exams must be completed within 90
days of the application date. The plumbing journeyman registration shall
specify the name of the person so registered, who shall thereby be authorized
to perform work as a plumbing journeyman.
   (c)   A plumbing apprentice registration shall be issued, without
examination, to beginners or plumbing apprentices employed by a person
registered as a master plumber with the City, upon application and payment of
the fee of twenty dollars ($20.00). The plumbing apprentice registration shall
specify the name of the person so registered, who shall thereby be authorized
to perform work as a plumbing apprentice.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956; Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-1981; Am. Ord. 2001-
119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2009-93, passed 12-1-2009; Am. Ord. O2010-89,
passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.04 EXPIRATION AND RENEWAL OF REGISTRATIONS.
   (a)   The registration of each master plumber shall expire on December 31 of
each year, but may be renewed by the person holding the same upon application
and payment of the renewal fee of fifty dollars ($50.00). Every master plumber,
upon each renewal of registration, must present a copy of their active State
license, a copy of a certificate of liability insurance verifying insurance in
the minimum amount as required by the Ohio Construction Industry Examining
Board in accordance with Ohio R.C. 4740.06(B) and listing the City of
Middletown as the certificate holder and a bond, as required in Section
1428.03, valid for the renewal period. The application for renewal and the fee
shall be filed with the Chief Building Official each year on or after November
1, but before January 1. If the registration has not been renewed on or before
December 31 it will expire. The holder of the registration may renew the
registration through January of the following year. Payment for renewal must be
received in the Building Inspection office by January 31. After January 31, the
master plumber must re-register in accordance with Section 1428.01(b) of this
chapter.
   (b)   The registration of each plumbing journeyman shall expire on December
31 of each year, but may be renewed, without examination, upon payment of the
renewal fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00). The fee shall be paid to the Chief
Building Official each year on or after November 1, but before January 1. If
the registration has not been renewed on or before December 31 it will expire.
The holder of the registration may renew the registration through January of
the following year. Payment for renewal must be received in the Building
Inspection office by January 31. After January 31 the plumbing journeyman must
re-register in accordance with Section 1428.01(c) of this chapter.
   (c)   The registration for each plumbing apprentice shall expire on December
31 of each year but may be renewed upon payment of the renewal fee of ten
dollars ($10.00). The fee shall be paid to the Chief Building Official each
year on or after November 1, but before January 1. If the registration has not
been renewed on or before December 31 it will expire. The holder of the
registration may renew the registration through January of the following year.
Payment for renewal must be received in the Building Inspection office by
January 31. After January 31, the plumbing apprentice must re-register in
accordance with Section 1428.01(d) of this ordinance.
(Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-81; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-01; Am. Ord.
O2009-93, passed 12-1-2009; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.05 TRANSFERABILITY.
   The registrations required by this chapter shall not be transferable.
(Ord. 3230, passed 12-26-1956; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.06 RECIPROCITY WITH OTHER MUNICIPALITIES.
   (a)   Any person registered as a plumbing journeyman by any other municipal
corporation of the State, upon payment of the prescribed fee shall be issued a
plumbing journeyman registration without examination.
   (b)   The provisions of this section shall not apply to registrants of
municipal corporations that do not waive similar requirements for registrants
of the City, nor shall they apply to an applicant for a registration who is
unable to provide satisfactory proof, as may be required by the City, that such
applicant is qualified to perform the contemplated work.
(Ord. 3454, passed 3-25-1959; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.07 REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF REGISTRATION.
   (a)   The Chief Building Official may review the registration of any
plumbing journeyman or plumbing apprentice under this chapter to determine
whether it should be revoked, be suspended or not be renewed; or that a
registration requested under this chapter not be issued to an applicant, if the
registrant or applicant has done any of the following:
      (1)   Been convicted of a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or a
felony;
      (2)   Violated any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules adopted
pursuant to it;
      (3)   Obtained the registration by means of fraud or misrepresentation;
or
      (4)   Been guilty of gross misconduct in pursuit of their profession.
   (b)   Upon becoming aware of circumstances or facts, which suggest that the
registrant or applicant has done any of the acts listed in divisions (a)(1)
through (a)(4) of this section, the Chief Building Official shall investigate
such facts or circumstances. If, after such investigation, the Chief Building
Official finds that there is probable cause to believe an act listed in
divisions (a)(1) through (a)(4) of this section has been committed by a
registrant or applicant, the Chief Building Official shall request that the
Board of Appeals review the registration or application for registration to
determine if the same should be revoked, suspended or not renewed, or whether
the application for registration should be denied. Notice of such request for
review shall be sent by ordinary mail delivery to the registrant or applicant
at the last address supplied by them. The notice shall include that a review
has been requested and a general statement of the grounds for proposed action.
The Board of Appeals shall conduct a review of the issues relating to the
registration or application in accordance with Chapter 1460 of this Title.
   (c)   (1)   If, after review, the Board of Appeals determines that grounds
exist for action to be taken regarding the registration or application, the
Board of Appeals may:
         A.   Revoke the registration; or
         B.   Suspend the registration; or
         C.   Refuse to issue or renew the registration.
      (2)   If the registration is revoked, the Board of Appeals shall
determine if the registrant may apply for reinstatement, and if so, when. The
Board of Appeals may require examination for reinstatement of a registration
issued by the City for plumbing journeymen.
   (d)   Nothing in this section is intended to limit the right of the City to
seek legal redress for violation of this chapter or any rules promulgated in
accordance with it.
   (e)   Upon becoming aware of circumstances or facts which suggest that a
master plumber has done any of the acts listed in divisions (a)(1) through (a)
(4) of this section, the Chief Building Official shall report such information
to the Ohio Construction Industry Examining Board for their review and action.
(Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.08 DISPLAY OF REGISTRATION AND REGISTRATION CARD.
   Holders of a master plumber registration shall keep said registration
displayed in a conspicuous place in their principal office or place of
business. All persons holding a master plumber, plumbing journeyman or plumbing
apprentice registration shall carry the registration card with them when on the
job site.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.09 DISPLAY OF NAME AND LICENSE NUMBER.
   All persons holding a master plumber registration shall identify all
business vehicles with the name of the registration holder and with the number
of their State license in letters/numerals not less than two inches high on the
exterior of the vehicle.
(Ord. O95-112, passed 10-3-1995; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.10 UNREGISTERED PERSONNEL ON JOB SITE.
   No registered master plumber shall permit any person employed by or working
for said master plumber, including subcontractors, to be working at the job
site unless registered with the City according to the provisions of this
chapter.
(Ord. 3675, passed 2-2-1961; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.11 EXEMPTIONS.
   (a)   This chapter shall not apply to departments, branches, service units
or buildings of the Federal or State government.
   (b)   A registration under the provisions of this chapter is not required of
the owner-occupant of a single-family dwelling who performs the work governed
by this Title Eight as to such dwelling, provided that such person obtains the
permits required in Chapter 1432 and submits such work for the inspections
required.
(Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1428.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the City from ordering that the work being performed
be stopped pending compliance with State and local laws, the enforced removal
of prohibited conditions or the application of any other equitable remedy.
(Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)

§ 1430.01 DEFINITIONS.
   (a)   UNDERGROUND UTILITIES CONTRACTOR'S WORK. Means and includes the work
of tapping public or main sewers, installing or connecting sanitary sewers,
building storm sewers, septic tanks and pertinent leaching systems, and
installing water service lines outside a building to the property or curb line.
   (b)   MASTER UNDERGROUND UTILITIES CONTRACTOR.  A person registered as a
master underground utilities contractor with the City. Only a master
underground utility contractor may apply for permits and be the representative
of the business entity in all matters relating to Title Eight of Part Fourteen
of the Codified Ordinances.
   (c)   UNDERGROUND UTILITIES INSTALLER. A person registered as an underground
utilities installer with the City. An underground utilities installer must be
working under the general direction and supervision of a master underground
utility contractor registered to work in the City. Underground utilities
installers cannot obtain permits.
(Ord. O92-53, passed 6-21-1992; Am. Ord. O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.02 REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   No person shall act as a master underground utilities contractor or
underground utilities installer in the City, without first registering with the
City in accordance with this Chapter.
   (b) A master plumber shall be entitled to do the work herein referred to
without taking an examination, provided said plumber possesses an active master
plumber registration issued by the City.
   (c)   Any person performing the physical underground utilities contractor
work on a job site and not holding a master underground utilities contractor's
registration from the City shall obtain a registration as an underground
utilities installer. Persons holding a plumbing journeyman or plumbing
apprentice registration and working under the supervision of a master plumber
will not be required to obtain an underground utilities installer registration.
   (d)   Any business entity engaged in underground utilities contractor's work
must have as a principal or in its employ a person registered with the City as
a master underground utilities contractor. Such person shall apply for all
permits and shall be the representative of the business entity in all matters
relating to Title Eight of Part Fourteen of the Codified Ordinances. If such
person should terminate or sever their relationship with the business entity,
such entity must cease all underground utility work unless and until another
principal or employee has obtained a registration as a master underground
utilities contractor from the City.
(Ord. 4307, passed 12-29-1965; Am. Ord. O92-53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord.
O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.03 REGISTRATION APPLICATION AND FEES.
   (a)   An applicant for a master underground utilities contractor's
registration shall be at least 21 years of age and shall have at least two
years of practical experience in performing underground utilities work as
defined in this chapter. A master underground utilities contractor registration
shall be issued to any person who has duly made application therefore and has
passed the examination with a minimum score of 70% as prescribed by the City.
Persons desiring to take the examination for a master underground utilities
contractor registration shall make written application therefore accompanied by
a fee of two hundred dollars ($200.00). Such fees shall not be refunded, but
any applicant failing the examination shall be entitled to one re-examination
without fee. Exams must be completed within 90 days of the application date.
After passing the exam the contractor shall present evidence that they are
insured in the minimum amount of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) for
damage to persons and property arising out of any negligent act of the insured
or any agent or employee of the insured and a bond approved by the Director of
Law in the penal sum of ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00). Such bond shall be
conditioned to reimburse the City for actual damages caused by act or omission
of the underground utilities contractor to any property and to hold the City
free and harmless from all claims for damages due to the negligence or
misfeasance of such master underground utilities contractor, or that may be
occasioned by reason of any opening made in any street, public land, alley or
avenue, in the making of any connection with any public or private sewer. Such
bond shall be in force from the date of its acceptance to the expiration date
listed on the bond and must be renewed annually. The proof of insurance shall
name the City of Middletown as the certificate holder. The master underground
utilities contractor registration shall specify the name of the person so
registered, who shall thereby be authorized to engage in the occupation of a
master underground utilities contractor.
   (b)   An underground utilities installer registration shall be issued,
without examination, to an underground utilities installer employed by a person
registered as a master underground utilities contractor with the City upon
application and payment of the fee of fifty dollars ($50.00). The underground
utilities installer registration shall specify the name of the person so
registered, who shall thereby be authorized to perform work as an underground
utilities installer.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-1981; Am. Ord. O92-
53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord. O2007-64,
passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2009-93, passed 12-1-2009; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed
12-21-2010)
§ 1430.04 EXPIRATION AND RENEWAL OF REGISTRATION.
   (a)   The registration of each master underground utilities contractor shall
expire on December 31 of each year, but may be renewed, without examination, by
the person holding the same upon application and payment of the renewal fee of
fifty dollars ($50.00). Every master underground utilities contractor, upon
each renewal of registration, must present a copy of a certificate of liability
insurance verifying insurance in the minimum amount of one hundred thousand
dollars ($100,000.00) and listing the City of Middletown as the certificate
holder and a bond as required in Section 1430.03, valid for the renewal period.
The applications for renewal and the fees shall be filed with the Chief
Building Official each year on or after November 1, but before January 1. If
the registration has not been renewed on or before December 31 it will expire.
The holder of the registration may renew the registration through January of
the following year. Payment for renewal must be received in the Building
Inspection office by January 31. After January 31, the master underground
utilities contractor must re-register in accordance with Section 1430.01(b) of
this ordinance, including all testing requirements.
   (b)   The registration of each underground utilities installer shall expire
on December 31 of each year but may be renewed upon payment of the renewal fee
of twenty-five dollars ($25.00). The fee shall be paid to the Chief Building
Official each year on or after November 1, but before January 1. If the
registration has not been renewed on or before December 31 it will expire. The
holder of the registration may renew the registration through January of the
following year. Payment for renewal must be received in the Building Inspection
office by January 31. After January 31, the underground utilities installer
must re-register in accordance with Section 1430.01(c) of this chapter.
(Ord. O81-73, passed 5-19-1981; Am. Ord. O92-53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord.
O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2009-93, passed 12-1-2009; Am. Ord. O2010-
89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.05 TRANSFERABILITY.
   The registrations required by this chapter shall not be transferable.
(Ord. 3230, passed 12-26-1956; Am. Ord. 2001-119, passed 11-6-2001; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.06 REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF REGISTRATION.
   (a)   The Chief Building Official may review the registration of any
underground utilities contractor or underground utilities installer under this
chapter to determine whether it should be revoked, be suspended or not be
renewed; or that a registration requested under this chapter not be issued to
an applicant, if the registrant, or applicant has done any of the following:
      (1)   Been convicted of a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or a
felony;
      (2)   Violated any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules adopted
pursuant to it;
      (3)   Obtained the registration by means of fraud or misrepresentation;
or
      (4)   Been guilty of gross misconduct in pursuit of their profession.
   (b)   Upon becoming aware of circumstances or facts, which suggest that the
registrant, or applicant has done any of the acts listed in divisions (a)(1)
through (a)(4) of this section, the Chief Building Official shall investigate
such facts or circumstances. If, after such investigation, the Chief Building
Official finds that there is probable cause to believe an act listed in
divisions (a)(1) through (a)(4) of this section has been committed by a
registrant, or applicant, the Chief Building Official shall request that the
Board of Appeals review the registration or application for registration to
determine if the same should be revoked, suspended or not renewed, or whether
the application for registration should be denied. Notice of such request for
review shall be sent by ordinary mail delivery to the registrant or applicant
at the last address supplied by them. The notice shall include that a review
has been requested and a general statement of the grounds for proposed action.
The Board of Appeals shall conduct a review of the issues relating to the
registration or application in accordance with Chapter 1460 of this Title.
   (c)   (1)   If after review, the Board of Appeals determines that grounds
exist for action to be taken regarding the registration or application, the
Board of Appeals may:
         A.   Revoke the registration; or
         B.   Suspend the registration; or
         C.   Refuse to issue or renew the registration.
      (2)   If the registration is revoked, the Board of Appeals shall
determine if the registrant may apply for reinstatement, and if so, when. The
Board of Appeals may require examination for reinstatement of a registration
issued by the City for master underground utilities contractors.
   (d)   Nothing in this section is intended to limit the right of the City to
seek legal redress for violation of this chapter or any rules promulgated in
accordance with it.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.07 DISPLAY OF REGISTRATION AND REGISTRATION CARD.
   Holders of a master underground utilities contractor registration shall keep
said registration displayed in a conspicuous place in their principal office or
place of business. All persons holding a master underground utilities or
underground utilities installer registration shall carry the registration card
with them when on the job site.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.08 DISPLAY OF NAME.
   All persons holding a master underground utilities registration shall
identify all business vehicles with the name of the registration holder in
letters not less than two inches high on the exterior of the vehicle.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.09 UNREGISTERED PERSONNEL ON JOB SITE.
   No registered master underground utilities contractor shall permit any
person employed by or working for said master underground utilities contractor,
including subcontractors, to be performing the actual physical work of an
underground utilities contractor at the job site unless registered with the
City according to the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.10 EXEMPTIONS.
   A registration under the provisions of this chapter is not required of the
owner-occupant of a single-family dwelling who performs the work governed by
this Title Eight as to such dwelling, provided that such person obtains the
permits required in Chapter 1432 and submits such work for the inspections
required.
(Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.11 SEWER CONNECTIONS; PERMIT REQUIRED; FEES.
   (a)   Any registered master underground utilities contractor or master
plumber desiring to tap any public sewer or water main shall procure a permit
therefor from the City Engineer.
   (b)   Any registered master underground utilities contractor or master
plumber desiring to install or connect a storm or building sewer or water line
shall first apply to and obtain from the Chief Building Official a permit to do
so.
(Ord. O92-53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord. O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.12 APPLICATION FOR PERMIT.
   All applications for the permits required in Section 1430.11 shall be in
writing signed either by the party employed to do the work as agent for the
owner, or by the owner, and shall state the location, name of the owner and
number of buildings to be connected.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord.
O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.13 NOTICE OF PROPOSED CONNECTION.
   After a permit to tap any sewer or drain within the City has been issued to
any registered master underground utilities contractor and prior to making any
such connection, it shall be the responsibility of the master underground
utilities contractor to determine that the sewer lateral is free from
obstruction and in a sound condition and to certify approval to the Division of
Inspection. No connection is to be made to any sewer lateral that is found to
be in such a condition as to prevent such certification of approval until the
City Engineer has been notified and all necessary repairs have been completed.
(Ord. 5310, passed 6-1-1971; Am. Ord. O92-53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord. O2007-
64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.14 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Chief Building Official shall make rules and regulations not
inconsistent with this chapter or the Ohio Plumbing Code for the installation,
connection and discharge of house sewers and private disposal systems. Such
rules and regulations shall be complied with by the property owner as a
condition to connecting his or her property to a house sewer or private sewage
disposal system. Rules and regulations for sewers and water services in the
public rights-of-way are contained in the City of Middletown Utility Rules and
Regulations.
(Ord. 4176, passed 5-24-1965; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004; Am. Ord.
O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.15 STREET CUT PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (a)   Before any permit is issued to make any connection under a street, the
master underground utilities contractor or master plumber shall first secure a
street cut permit from the Engineering Division and pay such reasonable fee as
is required for paving restoration. Such permit shall also be conditioned upon
compliance with any rules or regulations and applicable City ordinances.
   (b)   The Department of Public Works shall have jurisdiction over that part
of a sewer service in the street, and the connection to the main sewer. The
work shall be done in accordance with the construction standards and
specifications as established by the City Engineer.
(Ord. 4176, passed 5-24-1965; Am. Ord. O92-53, passed 6-2-1992; Am. Ord. O2007-
64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)
§ 1430.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to preclude the City from ordering that the work being performed
be stopped pending compliance with local laws, the enforced removal of
prohibited conditions or the application of any other equitable remedy.
(Am. Ord. O2007-64, passed 9-4-2007; Am. Ord. O2010-89, passed 12-21-2010)

§ 1432.01 PERMIT FOR PLUMBING REQUIRED; INSPECTION.
   (a)   No person shall do any plumbing work (as defined in §
1428.01) in the City, except in cases of repairs or leaks, without a permit
being first issued therefor by the Superintendent of Inspection. Applications
for permits shall be made on blank forms provided by the Superintendent, by the
owner of the property or by the master plumber contracting for the work.
   (b)   Unless otherwise specified, permits shall be required for all new
work, regardless of its size or character, and for all work of remodeling,
extension, alteration or reconstruction. A permit is also required for all
systems of plumbing changed from cesspool or septic tank to sewer, and such
plumbing systems shall he inspected and tested in such manner as will insure
the efficiency of the system. A permit is required for the replacing of any old
plumbing fixture or water heater.
   (c)   Permits shall not be required for the repairing of any old fixture,
faucet or valve to be used for the same purpose, for forcing out stoppage, or
for repairing leaks or relieving frozen pipes or fittings. However, such
repairs or alterations shall not be construed to include cases where new
vertical or horizontal lines of soil, waste, vent or interior leader or
conductor pipes are used or their relative locations changed, provided that, in
a building condemned by the proper authorities because of unsanitary conditions
of the house drainage or plumbing, no such drainage or plumbing shall be
considered as coming under the head of repairs, but all such house drainage or
plumbing shall be done as in the case of new buildings, and shall require a
permit.
   (d)   All plumbing, including the building sewer and water supply systems,
shall be inspected by the Superintendent to assure compliance with the
provisions of Chapter 1426 and all other applicable City ordinances, rules and
regulations.
(Ord. 5309, passed 6-1-1971)

§ 1432.03 APPROVAL OF PLANS; EMERGENCIES.
   (a)   No permit shall be issued until plans showing compliance with the
requirements of Chapter 1426, or a description of the work to be done, have
been submitted to the Superintendent of Inspection in duplicate.
   (b)   In cases of emergency, the applicant may proceed with the work and
file the application for a permit within twenty-four hours thereafter,
Saturdays, Sundays and holidays excluded.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1432.04 EXPIRATION OF PERMIT.
   If work is not begun under the approved plans within six months from the
date of approval, such approval shall be deemed to have expired by limitation.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1432.05 SPECIAL SUPERVISION.
   (a)   Where work covered by the plans required in §
1432.03 involves construction or building service equipment that is hazardous
or complex, or for other good reason requires special or expert supervision,
the architect who signed such plans or professional engineer who affixed his or
her seal thereto, or made the plans or computations for such work, shall
supervise the work and be responsible for its conformity with the plans as they
relate to safety and sanitation. Where the architect or professional engineer
is not available, another architect or professional engineer, or other
qualified person, shall perform the required supervision.
   (b)   Where such special supervision has been performed, the person
performing it shall make and file with the Superintendent of Inspection a
certificate that he or she has done so and that the completed work conforms
with the plans. Such certificate may be in lieu of inspection by the
Superintendent, provided that this section shall not be construed to deprive
the Superintendent of jurisdiction over the inspection of the work or to
prohibit him or her from making inspection, should he or she feel that such
inspection is necessary to assure compliance with the plans therefor.
(Ord. 4216, passed 7-6-1965)
§ 1432.06 RECORDS.
   The Superintendent of Inspection shall keep a record of all plans and
descriptions submitted to him or her under the provisions of this chapter,
together with his or her action thereon.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1432.07 DEVIATION FROM PLANS.
   Should the person making inspection under this chapter, in the process of
inspection, observe any deviation from the plans or description or any
noncompliance with any requirements of this Title, he or she shall immediately
order the work stopped, and shall give written notice to the person performing
the work, setting out the deviation or irregularity and ordering him or her to
correct the same. The work shall not recommence until the irregularity or
deviation has been corrected.
(Ord. 3232, passed 10-24-1956)
§ 1432.08 REMEDY FOR DEFECTIVE WORK.
   If the person making inspection under this chapter finds a defect in any
work, he or she shall notify the installer in writing to remedy such defect
within a stated reasonable number of days. No person shall fail to comply with
such notice.
(Ord. 5309, passed 6-1-1971)
§ 1432.09 DISCHARGE OF EFFLUENT.
   (a)   No person shall install any pump, piping, device, apparatus or other
system for discharging sump pump effluent into a public right of way until he
or she has first obtained a permit from the Commissioner of Inspection.
   (b)   The Commissioner of Inspection shall issue a permit if the requested
plan substantially conforms with one of the following modes of construction:
direct connection to a public storm sewer; direct discharge into a natural
drainage ditch; connection to a yard inlet; extension of a publicly maintained
sump pump outlet collector line from the nearest terminal of a public storm
sewer system; connection to a catch basin; discharge into a drainage swale; or
direct connection to a public storm drainage culvert.
   (c)   The discharge of sump pump effluent onto a public street surface or
gutter is specifically prohibited.
(Ord. O78-137, passed 7-18-1978)
§ 1432.10 WAIVER OF CERTAIN FEES.
   Fees shall be waived for any building or structure or portion thereof
erected by the State or any agency thereof, or by any political subdivision of
the State or any agency of any such political subdivision, except that fees for
one, two and three-family dwellings shall not be waived. Such waiver of fees
shall not be deemed a waiver of plan review and permit requirements.
(Ord. O83-34, passed 4-5-1983; Am. Ord. O2004-20, passed 3-2-2004)
§ 1432.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.

   Billposting - see GEN. OFF.

§ 1434.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   COLLAPSIBLE AWNING. Any roof-like structure attached to a building and
projecting over a thoroughfare, so constructed and erected as to permit its
being rolled or folded back to a position flat against the building.
   (b)   FIXED AWNING. Any rigid roof-like structure other than a marquee
attached to a building in an immovable position and projecting over a
thoroughfare.
   (c)   CANOPY. Any roof-like structure having a rigid frame erected over an
entrance to a building and attached to a building and attached to such building
in such manner as not to become an integral part thereof.
   (d)   MARQUEE. Any other permanent roof-like structure attached to the
building and becoming an integral part thereof.
(Ord. 3233, passed l0-24-1956; Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
§ 1434.02 COMPLIANCE WITH CHAPTER.
   No person shall erect upon, hang from or attach to any building or other
structure, any awning, canopy or marquee of any kind or nature over and across
the space or area occupied by a sidewalk or thoroughfare of the City in an area
designated for zoning as a BC (Business Center) District or a UC (Urban Core)
District except as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
§ 1434.03 INDEMNITY REQUIRED.
   The building permit to erect, hang or attach an awning, canopy or marquee
shall only be given and granted upon condition that the owner of the property
upon which such awning, canopy or marquee is to be erected or hung or to which
it is to be attached, and the applicant for permission to erect, hang or attach
such awning, canopy or marquee shall jointly and severally agree to indemnify
the City against loss or damage to persons and property that may result by
reason of the erection, hanging, attaching and maintaining of such awning,
canopy or marquee and by reason of the falling down, blowing down or removal of
such awning, canopy or marquee.
(Ord. 3233, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
§ 1434.04 PROJECTION AND HEIGHT.
   (a)   Projection over thoroughfare. No fixed awning shall project over a
thoroughfare a distance greater than 66 inches. No canopy or collapsible awning
shall project over a thoroughfare beyond a point twelve inches inside the curb
line, except that a collapsible awning, the lowest portion of which is not less
than 20 feet above the surface of a thoroughfare, may project beyond the curb
line, provided that the projection over the thoroughfare does not exceed 48
inches. The horizontal clearance between a marquee and the curb line shall be
not less than two feet.
   (b)   Height above sidewalk.
      (1)   The minimum distance between the lowest portion of an awning or
canopy and the surface of the sidewalk shall be as follows:
 
Type of Awning or Canopy Distance
Collapsible awnings      7-l/2 feet
Fixed awnings            8
Canopies                 9
 
      (2)   A marquee projecting more than two-thirds of the distance from the
property line to the curb line shall be not less than 12 feet above the ground
or pavement below.
      (3)   A marquee projecting less than two-thirds of the distance from the
property line to the curb line shall be not less than ten feet above the ground
or pavement below.
      (4)   A marquee projecting less than two feet beyond the property line
shall be not less than eight feet six inches above the ground or pavement
below.
(Ord. 3233, passed 10-24-1956; Am. Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
§ 1434.05 COMPLIANCE WITH OTHER LAWS.
   Any awning, canopy or marquee constructed in accordance with this chapter
must also comply with all other state and local building codes.
(Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
§ 1434.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than one
hundred dollars ($100.00). A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012)
CHAPTER 1436: PROPERTY MAINTENANCE
Section
Editor’s note:
   This chapter, previously a codification of Ord. 4042, passed May 18, 1964,
Ord. 4323, passed February 21, 1966, and Ord. O76-131, passed June 15, 1976,
and titled “Dangerous Buildings,” was re-titled “Property Maintenance” upon the
adoption of Ord. O99-118, passed October 19, 1999 (Chapter 1486 of these
Codified Ordinances). Subsequently, on the adoption of Ord. O2012-21, passed
June 19, 2012, Chapter 1486 was repealed, and this chapter was amended to adopt
the International Property Maintenance Code.
1436.01   International Property Maintenance Code adopted.
1436.02   Declaration of nuisance.
1436.03   Appeals.
1436.04   Repair of buildings or structures.
1436.05   Failure to comply with notices and/or orders.

§ 1436.01 INTERNATIONAL PROPERTY MAINTENANCE CODE ADOPTED.
   (a)   Pursuant to
Article IV, § 6, of the City Charter, there is hereby adopted by and for the
City, for the purpose of establishing rules and regulations and providing
minimum maintenance standards for all existing structures and on all existing
premises, that certain code known as the International Property Maintenance
Code, 2009 edition, promulgated by the International Code Council, Inc., save
and except such portions as may be hereinafter amended or deleted.
   (b)   Any conflict between the International Property Maintenance Code, as
adopted in §
1436.01, and the existing sections of these Codified Ordinances, shall be
resolved in favor of the more restrictive provisions. However, nothing in the
International Property Maintenance Code, as adopted in §
1436.01, shall be construed to limit or reduce the power of any official of the
City or the State in the enforcement of other codes of the City or the State,
including, but not limited to, zoning codes, fire codes, health codes and
building codes, or to reduce the requirements imposed by such codes.
   (c)   All references in the International Property Maintenance Code, as
adopted in §
1436.01, to the “code official” shall be construed to be the Chief Building
Official of the City. All fees to be charged in connection with the
International Property Maintenance Code shall be those set forth in the
specific sections of these Codified Ordinances. All appeals from decisions of
the Chief Building Official shall be in the manner and form set forth in the
specific sections of these Codified Ordinances.
   (d)   At least one copy of the International Property Maintenance Code, as
adopted in §
1436.01 shall be on file in the office of the Clerk of the City Council for
inspection by the public.
   (e)   The International Property Maintenance Code, as adopted in §
1436.01, is hereby amended as follows:
      Section 101.1   Title: Insert: City of Middletown.
      Section 107.3   Method of Service. Such notice shall be deemed to be
properly served if a copy thereof is:
      1.   Delivered personally;
      2.   Sent by certified mail addressed to the tax mailing address or agent
mailing address, evidenced by return receipt signed by any person.
      3.   Posted in a conspicuous place on or about the involved property and/
or structure, with a copy sent by regular mail addressed to the tax mailing
address or agent mailing address.
      Section 304.14   Insect screens: Every door, window and other outside
opening required for ventilation of habitable rooms, food preparation areas,
food service areas or any areas where products to be included or utilized in
food for human consumption are processed, manufactured, packaged or stored,
shall be supplied with approved fitting screens of not less than 16 mesh per
inch (16 mesh per 25 mm) and every swinging door shall have a self-closing
device in good working condition.
      Exception: Screens shall not be required where other approved means, such
as air curtains or insect repellants fans, are employed.
      Section 602.3   Heat supply: Every owner or operator of any building who
rents, leases or lets one or more dwelling unit, rooming unit, dormitory or
guestroom on terms, either expressed or implied, to furnish heat to the
occupants thereof shall supply heat to maintain a temperature of not less than
68°F (20°C) in all habitable rooms, bathrooms and toilet rooms.
      Exceptions:
      1.   When the outdoor temperature is below the winter outdoor design
temperature for the locality, maintenance of the minimum room temperature shall
not be required, provided that the heating system is operating at its full
design capacity. The winter outdoor design temperature for the locality shall
be indicated in Appendix D of the International Plumbing Code.
      2.   In areas where the average monthly temperature is above 30°F (-1°C),
a minimum temperature of 65°F (18°C) shall be maintained.
      Section 602.4   Occupiable work spaces: Indoor occupiable work spaces
shall be supplied with heat to maintain a temperature of not less than 65°F
(18°C) during the period the spaces are occupied.
      Exceptions:
      1.   Processing, storage and operation areas that require cooling or
special temperature conditions.
      2.   Areas in which persons are primarily engaged in vigorous physical
activities.
      Chapter 8 REFERENCED STANDARDS: The referenced standards are in the
following codes adopted by the City:
      1.   Ohio Building Code, the current edition adopted by the State of Ohio
(adopted in
Chapter 1404 of the Codified Ordinances).
      2.   Residential Code of Ohio, the current edition adopted by the State
of Ohio (adopted in
Chapter 1402 of the Codified Ordinances).
      3.   Ohio Fire Code, the current edition adopted by the State of Ohio
(adopted in
Chapter 1604 of the Codified Ordinances).
   (f)   The following sections of the International Property Maintenance Code,
as adopted in §
1436.01, are hereby specifically excluded from adoption: 103.1, 103.2, 103.3,
103.5, 111.1, 111.2, 111.3, 111.4, 111.5, 111.6, 111.7, 111.8, 302.4, 302.8,
and 308.
(Ord. O2012-21, passed 6-19-2012; Am. Ord. O2024-45, passed 7-2-2024)
